Selling a house in Atlanta

Atlanta homeowners can hire a listing agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase of the house in its present condition. The city has 242 officially defined neighborhoods and sits in two counties, so the right route depends on the block, the shape of the house and which tax office bills it.

  • An agent suits houses in neighborhoods where buyers expect staging and professional photos.
  • A private sale is realistic when you can price from comparable sales and handle the closing paperwork.
  • A cash sale as is helps with inherited homes, worn-out rentals, repair-heavy houses and owners facing a hard deadline.

Atlanta is the Fulton County seat and spills into DeKalb County. Before you list, find out which county holds your parcel, because that decides who assesses it, who bills it and which clerk records your deed.

Atlanta housing numbers

Atlanta had 529,110 residents in mid-2025, up 6.1 percent from 498,805 in 2020. Owners live in fewer than half of Atlanta homes, and the typical household is two people, so rental and small-household housing makes up a large share of the stock.

Citywide middles hide a wide spread. Prices swing a great deal from one of the 242 neighborhoods to the next, so use recent sales near your address as the real guide.

Neighborhoods and how buyers search

Three high-rise districts line up along Peachtree: Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead. Downtown has the metro area's largest office inventory, Midtown is the second-largest business district and a hub for arts and universities, and Buckhead, eight miles north of Downtown, ranks third.

Around them lie lower-density neighborhoods where the craftsman bungalow dominates. The eastside has streetcar suburbs built from the 1890s to the 1930s, among them Victorian Inman Park. Former warehouses along the Beltline and in West Midtown now hold housing, shops and galleries. In southwest Atlanta, areas near Downtown such as the West End began as streetcar suburbs, while Collier Heights and Cascade Heights keep a postwar suburban layout.

Emory University and the CDC area joined the city through an annexation effective January 1, 2018. Buyers search by neighborhood name, so put yours in the listing headline.

Which county taxes your house, and how to appeal

It depends on which side of the county line the parcel sits. Most of the city lies in Fulton County, whose Board of Assessors mails a notice each year and gives you 45 days from its date to respond. A DeKalb-side owner should read the notice from DeKalb County and ask that county's assessors about the deadline.

  • In Fulton, the dispute can cover value only, and the deadline printed on your notice governs.
  • You can file online, by mail, or at the Board of Assessors office, 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018.
  • The form offers a hearing, arbitration or a hearing officer, and a temporary bill may arrive in the meantime.

If you are mid-appeal when you sell, tell the closing attorney so the settlement statement can reflect any temporary tax bill.

Short-term rental rules

If you have rented the house by the night, the rules affect your sale. The city council passed its short-term rental ordinance, 20-0-1656, on March 15, 2021, and the rules took effect March 1, 2022. An owner or long-term tenant may hold a license for a primary residence plus one additional dwelling unit, and the license number must appear on every advertisement.

Hosts apply through the online permitting portal, which accepts applications daily. License appeals go to the Department of City Planning, and questions can go to STR@atlantaga.gov. Enforcement dates and implementation details can change, so confirm the current status with City Planning before you describe the house as a rental. Then tell buyers plainly whether the license can transfer.

Demand drivers: jobs and schools

The metro economy is the eighth largest in the country, and the city claims the nation's third-largest concentration of Fortune 500 companies. Coca-Cola, Home Depot, Delta Air Lines, UPS, Chick-fil-A and Norfolk Southern all have headquarters or hubs in the region. Delta, based at Hartsfield-Jackson, is the metro area's largest employer.

Georgia Tech in Midtown, Georgia State Downtown, Emory and the Atlanta University Center keep rental and starter-home demand steady in the center of the city. About 49,000 students attend 106 Atlanta Public Schools campuses, and private options include Westminster, Lovett, Pace Academy and Paideia. School questions come up early with buyers, so be ready with the zone for your address.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Atlanta houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Pricing in changing neighborhoods

Many in-town streets look different from how they did a few decades ago. After neighborhood opposition stopped two freeways planned through the east side in 1975, that area became the starting point for the gentrification that later spread. Atlanta's selection for the Olympic Games brought infrastructure work that pushed investment into other parts of the city, and construction of the Beltline has spurred new building along its path.

On blocks like these, neighbors and sale prices may have changed several times in a few years, which makes recent nearby sales the most useful pricing guide. One street can mix older bungalows with newer construction, so match your comparables by age and condition, not just by distance.

Trees, rain and traffic

Atlanta's humid subtropical climate brings hot summers and winters that are mild but variable, with about 50 inches of precipitation a year. The city is nicknamed the City in a Forest for its dense tree cover, so inspectors look hard at roofs, gutters and drainage near the foundation.

I-20, I-75 and I-85 meet here, and the combined I-75/85 Downtown Connector carries more than 340,000 vehicles a day. The I-285 Perimeter divides Inside the Perimeter from Outside the Perimeter, and buyers often search by that label. MARTA runs buses, heavy rail and a downtown loop, which matters to buyers who plan to skip the commute by car.

Transfer tax and recording

Georgia's transfer tax has to be paid before an Atlanta deed can be recorded. It is $1 for the first $1,000 of price or fractional part, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part. The seller is liable unless the contract says the buyer will pay.

Because Atlanta spans two counties, the superior court clerk who records your deed is the one for the county holding the parcel. The electronic PT-61 filing runs through the clerks' authority, and questions about exemptions go to the county clerk. Your closing attorney normally files the form for you.

Frequently asked questions

Which county handles my Atlanta property tax appeal?

The county the parcel sits in. Fulton County gives 45 days from the notice date, and DeKalb County sets its own procedure for the DeKalb part of Atlanta.

Do I need a license to rent my Atlanta house by the night?

Yes. The city's ordinance requires a short-term rental license, shown on every advertisement, and applications go through the online permitting portal.

What is the middle value of an Atlanta owner-occupied home?

The 2020 to 2024 survey shows $439,600. Prices vary a great deal among the 242 neighborhoods.

Who owes Georgia's transfer tax in an Atlanta sale?

The seller by default, though a contract clause can pass the cost to the buyer.

Can an occupied Atlanta rental be sold?

Yes, with the tenant and lease in place or after the lease ends. Review the lease terms before arranging showings.

Selling a Columbus house when time is short

With a deadline looming, a Columbus owner has three doors to try: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash buyer willing to take the place with every flaw. The calendar tends to pick the door.

Fort Benning is a major employer here, and plenty of local owners are working against a set move date. A cash buyer can name a closing day and bypass appraisal and lender steps, though the amount falls below retail. Houses in a downtown historic district or a newer Northside subdivision may bring a better price in a full listing, if waiting through showings and loan approval fits your schedule.

  • Agent: widest audience and the best shot at top price, but you handle cleanup, showings and loan contingencies.
  • On your own: keep the commission, take on the ads and the contract work.
  • Cash buyer: closing day fixed in advance, no repair list, a lower number.

Ask each bidder for written terms, then put the offers side by side and see which one leaves the most in your account after costs.

Columbus areas and buyers

Columbus merged with Muscogee County in the early 1970s and stands on the Chattahoochee River facing Phenix City, Alabama, roughly 100 miles from Atlanta, to the southwest. Fort Benning occupies land to the south.

The city divides into Downtown (also called Uptown), East Columbus, MidTown, North Columbus and South Columbus. MidTown is home to Aflac's headquarters, and South Columbus lies next to the National Infantry Museum. Wesley Woods, Leesburg and Windsor Park date from the late 1960s and early 1970s, built for returning troops and post families, and commercial growth later spread north along the I-185 corridor.

Aflac, TSYS, Synovus, Realtree and W. C. Bradley are headquartered here, and Columbus State University anchors higher education. The July 2025 estimate is 202,171 residents spread over 216.50 square miles of land, down 2.3 percent from 2020. Summers are hot. Know the age of your air conditioning and your roof, because buyers will ask.

Columbus housing numbers

Roughly half of Columbus homes (50.8 percent) have an owner living in them. An owned home is worth $193,900 at the middle, monthly rent is $1,106, and the middle household income is $58,073.

Columbus homes and rents, 2020 to 2024 data
Housing measureColumbus
Owner-occupied share50.8%
Typical owned-home value$193,900
Owner monthly cost, mortgage$1,489
Owner monthly cost, paid off$477
Middle gross rent$1,106
Households81,415

The city and Fort Benning are closely tied, and many sellers and buyers move on military schedules. Any buyer who finances will bring an appraisal and lender conditions that a cash buyer would not.

Schools and the Fort Benning line

The Muscogee County district serves the city with 35 elementary schools, 12 middle schools and nine high schools for over 31,000 students. Fort Benning is the exception for lower grades.

Children of families living on post attend schools run by the Department of Defense Education Activity through eighth grade, then to the public high school serving the county that holds the housing. A seller near the base should tell buyers which side of the line the address falls on, since families ask early.

Assessment notices and appeals

Each May the county's assessors send owners a notice of value, and the clock for objecting runs 45 days from the date on it. Taxes are computed on 40 percent of market value, with the city council choosing the mill rate.

Appeals start with the assessors, who route them to the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration. A hearing officer hears only non-homestead real property of $500,000 or more. The assessors are at 3111 Citizens Way. Filing an appeal does not pause the billing schedule, so pay the bill on time.

Due dates, homestead and deferral

The Tax Commissioner's bill arrives in August and is split, with 40 percent (or everything) due October 1 and the balance December 1. The Tax Commissioner can be reached at 706.653.4211.

  • Standard homestead: $13,500 off assessed value for maintenance and operation levies.
  • What to bring: the recorded deed and a Georgia license showing your address, with voter and vehicle registration in Muscogee.
  • Deferral: available to owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less.

Muscogee also offers a valuation freeze option. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether your parcel carries one before you quote a tax figure to a buyer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Columbus houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who owes the year's tax when a house sells

Whoever holds title on January 1 owes that year's tax in full, even when the house closes in March or October. After a spring or summer sale, a bill may reach both the seller and the buyer, which confuses people. The Tax Commissioner leaves the split to the parties, so look for the proration line on your settlement statement.

Should a bill go unpaid, the lien lands on the January 1 owner unless that person shows within 90 days of the due date that the buyer assumed the tax. Acceptable proof is a recorded deed in the buyer's name together with closing-document language handing the tax to the buyer.

What to gather and how a cash sale differs

Before you list or take an offer, collect your latest notice of value, the recorded deed, the current tax bill, any lease with the rent record, and permits for past work. Then ask the Tax Commissioner what is still owed so the year's tax can be prorated on the settlement statement.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal and the lender's conditions, so the closing date is yours to set. That suits owners with orders to move, an inherited house in Muscogee County, or a rental with problems a lender's appraiser would flag. A regular listing may bring a higher price, but it also brings inspection requests and a loan that can fall through. Compare offers by what you would take home after commission, repairs and the carrying cost of waiting, and ask each buyer for proof of funds and a written closing date.

Deed recording and transfer tax

Nothing gets recorded at the Muscogee clerk of superior court until Georgia's transfer tax has been paid. The law puts the cost on the seller, yet many contracts shift it to the buyer, so look at that clause. Your closing attorney normally pays the tax and files the required state transfer declaration as part of the closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Permits and code rules

The Inspections and Code Department applies the Georgia State Minimum Construction Codes for building, plumbing, electrical, mechanical and property maintenance. It reviews plans, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and schedules inspections.

The same department enforces the Unified Development Ordinance, which bundles zoning, environmental and subdivision rules. If your lot has a second structure or an unusual use, read it before you list, since zoning problems can surface in a buyer's due diligence. Also ask the department about any open permits on the house before a buyer's inspector goes looking for them.

Frequently asked questions

Is Columbus a city or a county?

Both at once. One consolidated government runs Columbus and Muscogee County, so the same tax offices handle every parcel.

What installment dates does the Muscogee tax bill follow?

October 1 for 40 percent of the bill (or all of it) and December 1 for the balance.

If I sell in June, who owes that year's tax?

Legally the January 1 owner. The closing documents decide how the cost is shared.

How much time do I get to dispute my Columbus value?

Forty-five days, counted from the notice date. Notices go out in May, and the written appeal goes to the assessors.

Is the seller charged a transfer tax in Columbus?

The seller is liable, although a contract may assign it to the buyer. Recording waits for payment.

Choosing how to sell in Augusta

A seller here can go the agent route, handle the sale privately, or let a cash buyer take the house untouched. Condition, calendar and the price cut you will accept for certainty usually settle the choice.

  • Agent route: the broadest exposure, with inspection haggling and a lender's schedule attached.
  • Private sale: the listing fee stays with you, and so does every chore.
  • Cash buyer: the fewest moving parts, with an offer shaped by the buyer's own repair and resale costs.

Whichever you pick, the assessment calendar, the local exemption and Georgia's transfer tax all apply, and each gets its own section below.

One government for city and county

The City of Augusta and Richmond County merged in 1996, and Augusta-Richmond County is one of only three consolidated governments in Georgia. A mayor and ten commissioners run it, and Hephzibah and Blythe stay independent inside the county lines. If your address is in one of them, ask which city charges also appear on your bill. In practice, one set of offices handles every parcel, so ask the tax commissioner what charges appear on yours.

Augusta is about 150 miles east of Atlanta along Interstate 20, and the Savannah River marks the border with Aiken County, South Carolina. Nine of its neighborhoods are on the federal historic register, and old neighborhoods mean old houses. If yours stands in a designated historic district, ask the city's preservation commission which exterior changes need approval before you pay for a pre-sale refresh.

Military, medical and college demand

Soldiers, doctors and students supply much of the local demand. Fort Eisenhower (formerly Fort Gordon), NSA Augusta and the Savannah River Site anchor a cybersecurity and advanced operations cluster.

  • Medical District: Augusta University Health, Piedmont Augusta and the Charlie Norwood VA.
  • Colleges: Augusta University, Augusta Technical College and Paine College.
  • Tournament week: the Masters is played during the first full week of April, and many owners rent their houses out for it.

Postings change on a fixed calendar. An owner who gets orders, or inherits a house from a relative stationed elsewhere, may have a short runway before mortgage and vacant-house costs add up.

Augusta housing numbers

Augusta-Richmond County had an estimated 201,999 people in mid-2025, barely changed from 202,081 in the 2020 census. Renting and owning split almost evenly, so landlords and tenants carry real weight in local sales.

These figures describe the whole consolidated area, so one house can land far from them. A local appraiser or agent can pull recent sales near your address. Many Augusta buyers are price-sensitive, so a house that needs work can lose more at retail than the repairs would cost.

Assessment notices and the appeal clock

Each owner gets a yearly assessment notice in the mail, and the appeal clock runs 45 days from the day it is issued. Nothing is due on the notice. It lists the assessed value, the exemptions on file and your appeal rights. The last day for appeals and homestead applications is printed right on it, so go by that date.

Senate Bill 566 changed the statewide notice layout, so the older tax estimate tables gave way to an Estimated Tax Savings section.

  • Use the Property Search tool at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com, or deliver the appeal by post, email or in person.
  • Written appeals only, filed before day 45.
  • Direct questions to the Board of Assessors at 706-821-2310, and keep a copy of whatever you file.

Homestead exemption

Augusta grants a local floating homestead exemption for qualifying primary residences, limiting certain increases in assessed value. April 1 is the yearly filing date. Owners who file late receive a reduced share: 66.67% for April 2 through 30, 58.33% during May and 50% on June 1. Tax bills typically arrive in August or September.

Because the exemption belongs to the owner who applied, it does not simply carry over to a buyer. Ask the assessors what happens to it when title changes. Your buyer will want to know what the tax bill will look like after the sale.

Transfer tax and recording

Georgia taxes the transfer itself, using the sale price: $1 covers the first $1,000, then 10 cents for every further $100 or fraction of $100. The liability falls on the seller, though a contract may hand the cost to the buyer. The Richmond County clerk of superior court will hold the deed unrecorded until the tax is paid.

The reporting form is PT-61, filed through the clerks' online portal, and whoever handles your closing usually files it. Ask the tax commissioner what is owed on the current-year bill so the cost can be split between buyer and seller on the settlement statement. If a deed might qualify for an exemption, ask the county clerk of superior court. For filing problems, the portal's support line is 800-304-5174.

What to gather before you list

Having paperwork ready shortens any sale. Pull together your latest assessment notice, a record of the exemptions on file, any lease and rent ledger if tenants live there, and receipts or permits for past repairs. If the house sits in a historic district, add whatever approvals the preservation commission gave for earlier exterior work.

Then walk through the steps in order. Get your parcel's county value from the Board of Assessors, collect two or three written offers or a listing price opinion, pick a closing attorney, and ask the tax commissioner for the current bill so the proration is settled before closing day. A cash sale skips the appraisal, the lender's underwriting and the repair negotiation, which is why it can close on a date you set. A traditional sale takes on all three, and any one of them can move the closing date or the price.

When a quick as-is sale makes sense

Speed pays off when waiting costs more than the discount a cash buyer applies. The discount is real, so gather several offers and read each term.

  • An inherited Richmond County house that no relative wants to carry.
  • A rental with a lease in force, or repairs a lender's appraiser would flag.
  • A move pinned to a base or hospital start date.
  • A house with code violations or liens that complicate a regular listing.

Request proof of funds, an offer in writing and a fixed closing date from every buyer. The Board of Assessors can also tell you the county's value for your parcel, a useful benchmark before anyone names a price.

Frequently asked questions

How many days does an Augusta owner have to contest an assessment?

Forty-five days from the issue date on the notice. Online, postal, email and in-person filing are all accepted, and the office line is 706-821-2310.

Does Augusta have separate city and county governments?

No. Augusta and Richmond County became a single government in 1996, while Hephzibah and Blythe remain separate cities inside the county. Ask the tax commissioner what charges appear on your parcel's bill.

Who bears Georgia's transfer tax in an Augusta closing?

By default the seller, though the sales contract can move it to the buyer. Recording waits until it is paid.

Can I sell an Augusta house that has tenants or damage?

Often yes, since a cash buyer accepts the house as it is. A regular listing can close with tenants too, but loan-backed buyers tend to request repairs, so compare what you would net on each path.

What is Augusta's population?

About 202,000. The mid-2025 estimate is 201,999 for the consolidated government, and the 2020 census recorded 202,081.

Which selling route suits a Macon owner?

Macon owners have three routes: an agent listing, a sale handled by the owner, or a purchase by a cash buyer. Weigh repair needs against the date you need funds.

  • Listing with an agent: usually the best price when the house shows well, with the longest timeline and the most preparation.
  • Selling on your own: keeps the agent's share of the price, while showings, contracts and buyer questions land on you.
  • Cash sale as-is: suits vacant, inherited, tax-delinquent or storm-worn houses, where repairs would cost more than the discount you give up.

With no mortgage involved, there is no lender appraisal to wait on. That helps when a house carries deferred repairs that an appraiser would flag.

Macon-Bibb housing at a glance

Macon is governed as Macon-Bibb County, a single consolidated government, so most local figures are county figures. The 2025 estimate is 157,556 residents, almost level with the 157,346 counted in April 2020. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $174,500, 51.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $1,066 a month.

At that price level, repair costs take a larger bite out of a sale than they would in a pricier market. Check any offer against sales close to your address, because one block can price very differently from the next.

Historic districts

Macon's older core affects what owners may do to a building. County Planning and Zoning has been updating design guidelines for the central business districts and the historic districts, including Intown, the Central Business District, Vineville and Cherokee Heights. Those guidelines cover exterior changes, new construction and demolitions.

If your house sits inside one of those districts, ask Macon-Bibb Planning and Zoning what review applies before you promise a buyer anything about exterior work, and before you agree to a repair credit that involves siding, windows or porches.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Macon house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Vacant or run-down houses and blight rules

The county takes abandoned and unsafe buildings seriously, and a vacant house left alone can pick up tax consequences or a demolition order. Under the county's blight program, a property counts as blight when it meets at least two listed criteria, such as being uninhabitable or abandoned, having severely overgrown vegetation at 12 inches or higher, or failing to meet code for at least one year after written notice.

An unkempt yard alone is not blight, and loose animals and abandoned vehicles go to other offices. For a property reported as blighted, the Office of the Mayor may send a "nuisance per se" letter, and the owner may then repair or demolish the structure. If the owner does neither, the county may proceed with demolition.

In the blight tax process the property must be vacant and the owner may appeal the designation. Properties not appealed can be placed on a list sent to the Tax Commissioner each August. Code Enforcement takes reports and completion notices at 478-803-0470.

An heir holding an empty house should deal with any notice early. Buyers who pay cash often reflect an open notice in the price instead of walking away.

Notice of assessment and appeals

Each spring the Macon-Bibb Board of Tax Assessors mails the owner of record a notice of assessment, as state law requires. The notice carries a 45-day window for a written appeal. The letter must name the appeal route you choose, and it must be hand delivered or mailed with a dated postmark, because emails and faxes are not accepted.

Either side may take a Board of Equalization decision to superior court within 30 days.

Homestead exemption and who to call

The county's September 2025 resolution puts the residential homestead exemption at $7,000. Officials also asked the local legislative delegation for added exemptions at ages 65, 75 and 85. A new local exemption needs a local act and a ballot vote, so ask the Board of Assessors whether the senior tiers are in effect before you count on them.

The Board is at 688 Walnut Street, Suite 200, phone 478-200-5550. The Tax Commissioner is at 610 Mulberry Street, phone 478-621-6500. Before fixing a closing date, call the Tax Commissioner for the live bill and any balance owed.

Georgia transfer tax on a Macon sale

Georgia taxes the transfer of title itself, and the Bibb clerk will not record the deed until payment is made. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 (or fractional part of $1,000), then 10 cents per extra $100 (or fractional part of $100).

By statute, O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10, the seller is liable, though sales contracts often shift payment to the buyer. Sellers complete a PT-61 form online through the state clerks' authority. Exemption questions go to the Bibb County clerk's office.

From first offer to closing day

  1. Settle or disclose any county notice about the building.
  2. Call the Tax Commissioner for the live bill and any balance, then give that figure to the closing attorney.
  3. Decide in writing whether you or the buyer pays the state transfer tax.
  4. Have the PT-61 filed and the deed delivered to the Bibb clerk for recording.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the repair demands that often follow one. A listing gives you the widest pool of buyers, but the buyer's financing sets the closing date. In either case, an open code notice or an unpaid tax balance is easier to fix before the offer than after it.

What to gather before selling

Pull together the deed, your latest assessment notice and tax bill, any code or blight letters, and mortgage payoff details. Add a list of repairs you already know about, so a buyer hears them from you first. Having these ready speeds up a cash offer and keeps a listed sale from stalling at closing.

Is a vacant Macon house with code problems still sellable?

Yes, though settle or disclose any county notice first. If Code Enforcement flagged blight, follow the letter and report completion at 478-803-0470, or tell the buyer about the open notice up front. Some cash buyers take the house with the notice open and adjust their price.

What is the deadline to contest a Bibb County value?

Forty-five days from the notice date, and the appeal must be on paper. Hand deliver the letter or mail it with a dated postmark, since email and fax are not accepted. Name your chosen route in the letter.

Does Macon-Bibb County offer a homestead exemption?

Yes, a $7,000 exemption on a residential homestead. The county also asked state legislators for extra exemptions at ages 65, 75 and 85, which need a local act and a ballot vote, so ask the Board of Assessors what applies to you.

Which party owes transfer tax on a Macon closing?

By statute the seller owes it, though the sales contract can hand the cost to the buyer. Read your contract, and ask the Bibb clerk about any exemption that might fit.

What documents should I gather before selling a Macon house?

Collect the deed, your latest assessment notice and tax bill, any code or blight letters, and mortgage payoff details. Add a list of repairs you know about.

Selling in Savannah?

Selling a house in Savannah

Savannah is the oldest city in Georgia and the Chatham County seat, and its low ground and historic core affect how houses change hands. The 2020 census counted 147,780 residents, with an estimate of 149,440 for 2025. The city sits on the Savannah River about 20 miles upriver from the Atlantic, and a steady base of renters, students and workers means a house you are selling may also appeal to a buyer who plans to rent it out.

Which neighborhoods and historic districts affect a sale?

More than 100 neighborhoods fall into six principal areas, and the label on your street changes what buyers expect.

  • Downtown: the Landmark Historic District and the Victorian District, built around the Oglethorpe Plan and its 22 squares.
  • Midtown: the central area between downtown and the Southside.
  • Southside: the southern part of the city, linked to downtown by the Truman Parkway.
  • Eastside and Westside: two more of the city's principal areas.
  • Southwest and West Chatham: suburban areas annexed more recently.

Besides the main Savannah Historic District, five other districts are formally marked: Victorian, Cuyler-Brownville, Thomas Square, Pin Point, and Ardsley Park-Chatham Crescent. If your house lies inside a district, phone the city's planning staff about review of exterior changes such as windows, siding or porches before you start work.

Flooding and storm history

Flood risk is the practical issue. Savannah is prone to flooding because of heavy rainfall, an elevation just above sea level and the shape of the coastline, and the city uses five canals and several pumping stations to manage flash flooding. Hurricanes have affected the area, among them Matthew in 2016, Irma in 2017, and Debby and Helene in 2024. Expect buyers to ask about water in the yard, crawl spaces and prior claims.

Gather what you have before listing: repair receipts, drainage work, any flood insurance paperwork, and photos from past storms. If the house has unrepaired storm damage, an as-is sale may fit better than a listing that requires a buyer's lender to approve the condition.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Savannah house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Can a former Savannah vacation rental be sold?

You can sell it, but Savannah regulates these rentals tightly. The city defines a short-term vacation rental as lodging in a residential unit for no more than 30 consecutive days, and renting a single room is regulated separately as a bed and breakfast homestay. Where rentals are allowed depends on location:

  • Inside the overlay district, which covers the Downtown, Victorian and Streetcar local historic districts.
  • Outside the overlay, only in the B-C, B-N, B-L and A-1 zoning classes.
  • In the Downtown and Victorian districts, new rentals in residential areas are capped at 20 percent of residential parcels in each ward, with owner-occupied parcels exempt.
  • Applications filed before September 28, 2017 were grandfathered and may be renewed.

The city's fees are $400 for a new application and $250 for annual renewal, both non-refundable, and applications go through the city's STVR registration portal. A buyer who plans to keep renting the house should contact the city office listed on the STVR page before closing to learn what the buyer must file.

City of Savannah property tax bills and late charges

The City of Savannah collects its own property tax in two installments, apart from the county and school bills. The city's Revenue Department sends the first bill in April, typically due in mid-June and based on half of the prior year's tax. The second goes out in September, typically due in mid-November, and reflects that year's value, exemptions and millage. Due dates are set when the bills are printed, so check the bill itself.

Only 40 percent of the appraised figure is taxable under state law, the appraisal comes from the Chatham County assessors, and anyone living in the city pays county tax and city tax. School board taxes are collected by the Chatham County Tax Commissioner. The city does not offer payment plans, and a payment is on time only if it posts to the account by the due date.

Billing step or penaltyRule
First installmentBilled in April, typically due mid-June, based on half of prior year
Second installmentBilled in September, typically due mid-November

Penalty5 percent once 120 days late, repeating every 120 days up to 20 percent

The Revenue Department's property tax unit, 912-651-6455, can supply a copy of any bill you did not receive, since a lost bill is no defense to a late fee.

Homestead exemption, appeals and tax sales

Homestead exemption applications go to the Chatham County Board of Assessors at 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue, Suite 113, and the phone number is 912-652-7271. To qualify, you must have owned the home and lived there as your permanent residence on January 1. Rentals are excluded. Filing by the 45-day appeal date on your annual notice covers the current year, and filing later covers the next.

An appeal must answer an annual assessment notice, and the window runs 45 days from the date it shows. The assessors measure square footage on file from the exterior perimeter, which often differs from the living area an owner measures inside, so check that before you argue.

If taxes stay unpaid, the city holds about six tax sales each year. An owner may redeem within a year and a day by paying the winning bidder the bid plus 20 percent. A seller who has fallen behind should clear delinquent tax and any Fi. Fa. lien before closing, since the lien must be satisfied for a clean title to pass.

Which routes sell a Savannah house fastest?

Owners here usually weigh three routes: an agent listing, an as-is investor sale, or a direct cash sale. A public listing can fetch the best price for a clean, updated house, though it brings open houses, inspections and a financing risk.

Selling for cash gives up some price in return for a firm closing date, which can suit houses with deferred repairs, tenants, probate or tax problems. Whatever route you choose, ask for the net figure after taxes, liens and closing costs, and verify every payoff before you sign.

Georgia's transfer tax also applies to the deed. Ask your closing attorney who pays it under your contract, and request a draft settlement statement early so you can check the tax line, the payoff and any lien release before closing day.

Frequently asked questions

When do Savannah city taxes come due?

The city's two installments are typically due in mid-June and mid-November. The exact dates are set when the bills are printed, so read your bill.

Can I still apply for homestead exemption if I miss April 1?

Yes, if you file by the 45-day appeal due date on your notice of assessment, the Board of Assessors considers it for the current year. Later applications apply to the following year.

Could my Savannah house be a vacation rental?

Only if it sits in the overlay district or one of the B-C, B-N, B-L or A-1 zones, and downtown residential areas face a 20 percent ward cap. Owner-occupied parcels are exempt from the cap.

What happens if I lose my house at a Savannah tax sale?

You can redeem within a year and a day by paying the winning bidder the bid amount plus 20 percent. Contact the bidder directly to arrange it.

Who decides what my Savannah home is worth for tax?

The Chatham County Board of Assessors does, and the city levies its own tax on that value. Appeals start with the notice of assessment and a 45-day window.

Your options for selling in Athens

Athens and Clarke County run as one consolidated government, so assessments, permits and short-term rental rules all come from Athens-Clarke County. You do not juggle a separate city hall and county office. From there you can list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or take a cash offer that skips repairs and open houses.

  • Listing with an agent: a good fit for houses near campus and in established neighborhoods that photograph well.
  • Selling it yourself: practical when you already know what nearby houses have sold for.
  • Cash sale as-is: often chosen for rentals with student tenants, inherited houses and properties that need work.

Whichever way you go, the steps are similar. Pick a price from recent nearby sales, gather the lease if tenants live there, get your latest assessment notice, and choose a closing attorney early. A cash buyer can close on the day you choose because no lender has to approve a loan. Ask for each offer in writing and compare what you would net after costs, not just the headline price.

Athens housing at a glance

Athens-Clarke County had 128,612 people in July 2025, up 1.0 percent from 127,357 in 2020. Renters outnumber owners here. Only 40.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and about 73 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, a low share that fits a university town. Plan on a buyer pool that includes investors as well as families.

These are countywide middles. A house near campus, a renovated bungalow and a dated ranch on the edge of town will each sit far from them, so ask for recent sales on your own street.

Student demand and the University of Georgia

The University of Georgia is the center of local rental demand, and Athens Technical College, a Piedmont University campus and the Augusta University and UGA medical partnership add more students and staff. For a landlord, that means steady interest in houses within reach of campus.

Pharmaceutical and biotechnology employers such as Boehringer-Ingelheim and Janssen Pharmaceuticals, along with technology firms, also draw workers who rent or buy in town. If you sell a rented house, hand each buyer the lease and its end date early. A sale can close with the tenant in place or after the lease ends.

Short-term rentals and a sale

If your house has been rented by the night, read this before you list. On February 6, 2024, the Mayor and Commission adopted amendments under Title 9 of the county code that define a short-term rental as lodging for transient guests for fewer than 31 consecutive days.

  • Home occupation STRs need an owner-occupant or a long-term tenant of the owner, and only one structure on the parcel can be used.
  • Commercial STRs are not limited that way but go through construction plans review.
  • Hotel-motel tax and a business occupation tax certificate apply, including a 7 percent local excise tax.

Properties on the Legal Non-Conforming STR List, finalized March 1, 2025, can keep operating for up to 24 months from that date. A change in ownership ends the non-conforming status. A buyer who plans to keep renting nightly must meet the ordinance as a new operator. Tell buyers this up front, and ask the Planning Department whether your parcel is on the list.

Homestead exemptions

Georgia's standard homestead exemption is $2,000. Athens-Clarke County goes further: its printed schedule gives $25,000 for the county operating levy and $10,000 for the school operating levy on the regular owner-occupied exemption. Separate codes cover seniors, low-income owners and certain disabled owners.

Both ownership and residence must be in place on January 1, and applications are taken in person at the Tax Commissioner's Office. The cutoff falls 45 days after assessment notices go out, which is usually mid-May. Late applications count for the following year. The county also offers a one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant on 2026 bills for owners who qualify.

Moving the house into a trust or adding a new spouse to the deed requires a fresh application, so ask the office before you change title on a house you still occupy.

How to appeal your assessment

The clock is 45 days from the date printed on your notice. Phone the assessors first and ask for the appraiser named there. Plenty of disputes get sorted out in that one call.

If the call settles nothing, put it in writing. The county accepts three grounds: value, uniformity or a denied exemption. You can pick the Board of Equalization, arbitration or, for certain properties above $500,000, a hearing officer. Bring recent sales of similar houses and photos of any condition problems. A high bill alone is not a ground.

Hills, weather and what buyers inspect

Athens sits on a string of Piedmont hills. Summers are sticky, winters range from mild to fairly cold, and about 46 inches of precipitation falls in a year. Spring thunderstorms can turn severe. On hilly lots, buyers and inspectors look closely at drainage, grading and roof condition, so repair or document these before showings.

For commuters, the SR 10 Loop forms a perimeter around town, and US 78, US 29, US 129 and US 441 all meet here. Athens Transit is fare-free, which appeals to student renters.

Describing your part of town

Buyers sort Athens by road and by distance to campus. Broad Street and Atlanta Highway split the city east to west, and Milledge Avenue splits it north to south. Prince Avenue runs through the Normaltown area, where a Piedmont University campus stands.

  • East side: College Station Road, Gaines School Road and Lexington Road (US 78).
  • West side: Epps Bridge Parkway, Alps Road and Timothy Road, meeting the Atlanta Highway corridor.
  • Parks: Sandy Creek Park covers 782 acres around the 260-acre Lake Chapman.

Say which road you are on and which school zone you fall in, in plain words, because both questions tend to come before any talk of price. A one-line note about the walk or drive to campus helps too.

Deed and transfer tax at closing

Before the Clarke County clerk will record your deed, the state's transfer tax has to be paid. It runs $1 on the first $1,000 of price, then 10 cents on every additional $100. By default the seller owes it, but many contracts hand it to the buyer, so read that clause.

The seller's side completes the PT-61 declaration online through the clerks' cooperative authority. Security deeds and certain leases need no PT-61 filing. If you wonder whether an exemption fits your transaction, ask the Clerk of Superior Court for Clarke County. Your closing attorney usually handles the filing and the recording.

Will my Athens house lose its short-term rental status if I sell?

It can. A change in ownership ends legal non-conforming status, so the new owner must comply with the short-term rental ordinance to keep renting nightly.

When is the Athens homestead deadline?

It falls 45 days after assessment notices go out, usually in mid-May. A late application is processed for the following tax year.

Does putting a spouse on my Athens deed affect the homestead exemption?

Yes. Moving the home into a trust or putting a new spouse on the deed requires a fresh application.

Where is the deed recorded for an Athens sale?

The Clarke County superior court clerk records it after the tax is paid and the PT-61 is filed.

Can I sell an Athens student rental with tenants still in it?

Yes. A rented house can sell with the lease still running or once it ends. Review the lease before arranging showings.

Who handles what in South Fulton

South Fulton is a young city with an unusual setup. It took over zoning, police, fire and code enforcement when it took effect on May 1, 2017, yet property valuation and tax billing still run through Fulton County. That split decides which office you call about each piece of a sale.

The 2020 census counted 107,436 residents, which made South Fulton the state's eighth-largest city. It was carved from southwest Fulton County and takes in many older communities that kept their names, such as Red Oak, Cooks Crossing, Fife, Ben Hill, Sandtown, Cliftondale, Cedar Grove, Enon and Welcome All. Buyers and agents still describe houses by those names. Confirm the tax district and zoning for your exact address before you sign anything.

The Old National Highway corridor is the city's main commercial street, with a large revitalization planned along it, so a seller nearby may hear questions about construction and future uses. Fulton County Schools serves the entire city, and the city runs no school district. Attendance boundaries can change by street, so point buyers to the school system's own address lookup instead of promising a school assignment in the listing.

Water, trash pickup, elections and public health are handled by Fulton County or private companies, not the city. If you hand a buyer a list of the house's services, name the county or company so the right office gets the call at closing.

Permits for repairs before a sale

The city's Development Services division, part of Community Development and Regulatory Affairs, handles permits, and applications are filed through the SagesGov portal. Permit staff can be reached at 470-809-7200, extension 1, between 8:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. The division processes these residential items:

  • New construction and demolitions
  • Alterations, additions and renovations
  • Sheds and fences
  • Retaining walls
  • Mechanical, electrical and plumbing trade permits

Inspections are scheduled in the same portal, and a request made before 4 p.m. can be conducted the next business day. State minimum construction codes now include the 2024 International Residential Code with Georgia amendments, so contractors should be working to the newer editions. If you plan only light repairs, call the permitting line before starting and ask whether the work needs a permit. Skipping that step can cause trouble when a buyer's inspector or the city's code staff notices.

Can I sell a South Fulton house that I rented short term?

Yes, but the permit status should be clean before you list. In 2025 the city dropped its Special Use Permit requirement for short-term rentals and replaced it with a standard permit application. The city defines a short-term rental as lodging for no more than 30 consecutive days, and rentals are allowed only in residential zoning districts.

The application can be emailed or dropped off at City Hall. A non-refundable $200 application fee is invoiced after the city receives and approves the application at intake. Running a rental without a valid permit may bring fines, penalties or suspension, and repeated violations can lead to denial of later applications. The city also posts a running list of permit applications marked approved, denied or pending, and it accepts public comment on pending ones.

South Fulton property taxes and appeals

The City of South Fulton states that its property taxes are billed and collected through the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, while the Board of Assessors sets value, accepts homestead applications and handles appeals. Recent notices of assessment show estimated tax savings rather than an estimated tax bill, following a change in state law.

An appeal must be filed within 45 days of the notice date, online, by mail or in person, and an appeal covers value only. When you file, choose a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration or a hearing officer. Fees may apply on some routes. A temporary bill can arrive while the appeal is open, and it still has to be paid.

Homestead applications filed after the April 1 deadline can be accepted during the appeal window for owners who held the home on January 1. The South Fulton Service Center for both the assessors and the tax commissioner is at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road. The assessors' phone line is 404-612-6440 and the tax commissioner's is 404-613-6100.

What a South Fulton seller should expect at closing

Plan on a deed recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court of Fulton County and a transfer tax payment tied to that recording. Questions about taxability and exemptions go to the clerk of the county where the property sits. Your closing attorney will also look for unpaid taxes and code liens, since both can delay a deed.

Owners who want a sure thing often line up an agent listing, an as-is investor sale and a direct cash sale side by side. Repairs, timing and the cash you need left over after liens and taxes will point to the winner.

Get a draft settlement statement a few days ahead of closing and read the payoff, tax lines and lien releases against your own records. Questions are easier to settle early. Even when a cash buyer skips loan approval, the deed, the transfer tax and the lien search still take place, and your attorney handles each one. Allow a little extra time if an open permit or a short-term rental record needs sorting out first.

Steps before you accept an offer

  1. Call the permitting line and ask about any past work that needed a permit or still has one open.
  2. Find out if the house was ever rented short term and where that permit stands.
  3. Ask the Fulton County offices for the current tax bill and any open balance.
  4. Collect an agent's opinion of value and a written cash offer, and compare the net after liens and taxes.
  5. Hand the closing attorney your deed and let the attorney search for liens early.

An investor paying cash can take on open permit items or a half-finished repair. A lender may refuse, which is why how you handle these loose ends decides which offers stay on the table, and a clear record also gives you a stronger hand in any price talk.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the property tax bill for a South Fulton house?

Fulton County does. The city says its taxes are billed and collected through the Fulton County Tax Commissioner.

How long do I have to appeal my South Fulton assessment?

You have 45 days from the date printed on the notice of assessment. After that deadline, your right to appeal that year's value is lost.

Do I need a Special Use Permit to run a short-term rental in South Fulton?

No. Since 2025 the city uses a standard STR permit with a $200 non-refundable application fee, and rentals are allowed only in residential zoning districts.

Can I fix up my house without a permit before selling?

Only for work the city does not regulate. Alterations, additions, renovations, sheds, fences and trade work such as electrical and plumbing go through the permitting division.

Which county office handles the deed when I sell?

Selling in Sandy Springs

Sandy Springs is an office-and-hospital suburb in northern Fulton County. Sellers deal with county offices for valuation and tax billing, and with city hall for permits. The city spans 38.52 square miles, and its population was 108,080 at the 2020 count with an estimate of 105,013 for 2025.

The city borders Atlanta to the south, Dunwoody and Brookhaven to the east, and the Chattahoochee River to the west and north. Hospitals and corporate offices make up much of the job base, so the buyer pool often includes people who work at the medical campuses or the Perimeter Center towers. Georgia 400, I-285, Roswell Road (U.S. 19) and Georgia 9 carry most traffic, and three MARTA rail stops serve the city: Medical Center, Sandy Springs and North Springs. Houses near the stations and the 400 and 285 interchange tend to be described by their commute, so give buyers an honest drive or ride time.

Neighborhood areas buyers ask about

One district can draw a very different buyer than another. The city's districts include:

  • City Springs: the downtown district north of I-285, with apartments replacing older strip malls along Roswell Road.
  • Riverside: the hilly western district along the Chattahoochee.
  • The Panhandle: a strip between the river and Dunwoody, reached from the Northridge Road exit of Georgia 400.
  • Perimeter Center: the commercial area around Perimeter Mall, including most office towers and the hospital cluster known as Pill Hill.
  • North Springs: the northern district served by the North Springs MARTA station.
  • South Springs: the part below I-285 that buyers call inside the Perimeter.

Know which district your house sits in and describe it plainly, whether the draw is the commute, the river or the school zone. Fulton County School System runs the public schools, and attendance zones differ by street, so buyers will check the exact address on the school system's lookup before making an offer.

Which repairs need a City of Sandy Springs permit?

Most structural work needs a residential building permit, issued by the permit desk at City Hall, 1 Galambos Way. Owners apply online, and a technician can meet you by appointment. The city's page sets out what triggers a permit and what does not:

  • A permit is required whenever an owner builds, alters, enlarges or repairs a building or accessory structure, and also for deck or patio replacements and generator installations.
  • Painting and carpeting generally need no permit.
  • Detached structures under 120 square feet need no building permit but may still face Development Code rules.
  • Flat roof replacement needs a permit; replacing individual shingles on a pitched roof does not.
  • Fire or storm repair within the original footprint falls under a reconstruction permit, and emergency stabilization may begin first if the permit is applied for within 48 hours or the next business day.

Contractors with a state license can pull permits, and so can an owner for the home where that owner currently lives. If you have been renting the house out, plan on hiring a contractor for anything beyond cosmetic work.

Fulton County assessments and tax bills

The county's Board of Assessors sets value, and the Fulton tax commissioner's office sends the bill that covers the county, the schools and the City of Sandy Springs. Notices go out each summer, owners get 45 days to appeal from the date of the notice, and filing works online, through the mail or at an assessors' office.

Homeowners who miss the April 1 homestead deadline can still apply during that 45-day appeal period. Because the bill attaches to the property for the whole year, anyone closing late in the year should decide in the contract who pays it and confirm with the closing attorney how it will appear on the settlement statement.

The North Fulton service center of the Board of Assessors is at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210, and the main phone line is 404-612-6440.

Who pays the Georgia transfer tax?

Title transfers in Georgia carry a state excise tax. The seller owes it, and many contracts move the cost to the buyer. The state sets the rate at a flat $1 on the first $1,000, then 10 cents for each further $100 or part of $100.

Payment comes first. Only then will the superior court clerk record the deed and stamp it as paid. The declaration, Form PT-61, goes in electronically through the clerks' cooperative authority, and exemption questions go to the Fulton County clerk. Check the transfer tax clause in your contract, since it decides who writes that check.

Can a former Sandy Springs short-term rental be sold?

Yes, and the first thing to settle is the city's lodging tax record. Sandy Springs requires hotels, motels and short-term rentals to collect occupancy tax from guests and remit it by the 20th of each month for the prior month, with a completed return. Returns paid on time earn a vendor credit of 3 percent of the tax collected. Late payments lose that credit and may carry penalties and interest.

If you operated a rental, file any missing returns and pay what you owe before you list, because a buyer's attorney may ask for proof. Mail goes to the Business Occupation and Excise Tax Division at 1 Galambos Way, and the Permits and Revenue Office at City Hall can help with filing. If the house sits in a subdivision, also read your association covenants, since they can restrict rentals separately from city rules.

Who handles which part of a sale?

Several offices touch a sale, and each answers a different question.

Where Sandy Springs sellers take each property question
QuestionOfficeDetail
Is my value fair?Fulton County Board of AssessorsAppeal window of 45 days after the notice
Who sends my tax bill?Fulton County Tax CommissionerCollects for the county, schools and Sandy Springs
Do I need a permit?City permitting office, 1 Galambos WayRequired for building, altering or repairing
Rental tax owed?Business Occupation and Excise Tax DivisionOccupancy tax due the 20th of each month
Who pays transfer tax?Georgia Department of RevenueSeller is liable unless the contract says otherwise

The realistic paths are a conventional listing, an as-is sale to an investor, or a direct cash sale when timing outranks top price. Compare net proceeds, not only the headline number. A direct cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and appraisal, which is why it can close sooner when title is clear. A listing can still net more for a house in good order, so ask for the figure after taxes, liens and closing costs from each route and read them side by side.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can a Sandy Springs house sell for cash?

A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, so it can close sooner than a listing when title is clear. A listing adds showings, inspections and the buyer's financing.

Do I owe transfer tax on a Sandy Springs sale?

Legally the seller owes it, though a contract can hand the cost to the buyer. The state's rate is a flat $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each further $100.

Can I appeal my Fulton value after listing?

Only during the 45 days after your notice was issued. When that window shuts, the year's value stands, so find the deadline on the notice itself.

What if I rented the house short term?

Pay any unpaid city lodging tax before closing. Monthly returns fall due on the 20th, and filing late gives up the 3 percent vendor credit.

Does a new roof need a permit before I sell?

A flat roof replacement needs one, but replacing individual shingles on a pitched roof does not. Call the city permitting office if your project falls in between.

The middle owner's home in Roswell is valued at $567,100 for 2020 through 2024, and owners occupy 71.9% of homes. Cash tends to win when something blocks the listing route: an estate with several heirs, tenants in place, worn-out systems, or a deadline from a lender or a move.

It covers 40.72 square miles, with about 2,280 people per square mile in 2020. The Roswell Historic District sits beside newer development, so age, lot and neighborhood weigh heavily when a buyer sizes up a house.

  • Tenure: owners live in 71.9% of homes among 35,540 households (2020-2024).

Your own sale still hinges on the street, the lot and the shape of the house.

Building permits and inspections

Roswell's Building Division, part of Community Development, applies the state minimum building codes through permits, plan review, inspections and certificates of occupancy. Every application goes through the Permitting and Licensing HUB online. Neither applications nor inspection requests are taken by email or phone.

Work done without a permit can stall a closing, since a lender or inspector may ask for the paperwork. The city's FAQ sets out when a permit is needed:

Work on a Roswell housePermit needed?
New deck, or replacing an existing deckRequired, with a site plan to check setbacks
Replacing a water heaterRequired, plus state licensing if a tradesperson does it
Swimming pool for a one- or two-family homeRequired, using the city's pool plan review checklist
Moving a house in, out or through the cityRequired, with a route map

A permit that expired less than 180 days ago can be reinstated by formal request, and the city issues a Certificate of Completion or Certificate of Occupancy after a final inspection passes. If a past contractor never closed a permit on your house, ask the Building Division what the record shows.

Know how inspections work before you hire anyone. The permit, job card and approved plans must be on site, the inspector needs access between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m., and someone must be present at an occupied home. Results are entered on a tablet at the site and emailed to the permit holder. A cancellation request goes through the account portal and is accepted when made the day before.

How to appeal a Fulton County assessment

Fulton County's Board of Assessors sends each Roswell owner a yearly notice of assessment. The notice starts a 45-day clock. Let it lapse and, in the county's words, the right to appeal is lost.

  • Scope: the assessed value alone; the estimated tax on the notice cannot be appealed.
  • Filing: the assessor's website, any of five county assessor offices, or the mail.
  • Three tracks: a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration limited to value, or a Hearing Officer. The last two may carry fees.
  • During the wait: review can run several months, and a temporary tax bill still has to be paid or penalties can follow.

North Fulton has a service center at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210, and the assessor line is 404-612-6440. A pending appeal touches the tax bill a buyer inherits, so tell the title company early.

What is filed when a Roswell sale closes?

Transfer tax comes first, and only then can a deed be recorded. The clerks' cooperative, GSCCCA, treats it as an excise on a sale that transfers title, and it hosts the online PT-61 form you print for the deed.

Each deed gets one PT-61. A Roswell filing lands in Fulton County through whoever runs your closing. Your contract decides who bears the tax, and the closing office can confirm the rate. Ask for a draft closing statement before the day, and check the payoff and tax lines against what you expect.

When does a cash offer suit a Roswell house?

Even in a high-value city, some houses do not fit a standard listing. Typical Roswell cases include:

  • An older house in a historic area with original systems that a financed buyer's inspector will flag.
  • A property held in an estate where heirs disagree on timing or cannot manage repairs.
  • A rental with tenants whose lease limits showings.
  • A seller facing foreclosure or a move date who needs to close on a known day.

Set the offer beside the likely listing net after commissions, repairs and carrying costs, and decide once the numbers are in front of you.

Steps before you list

  1. Ask the Building Division whether any permit on the house is still open or has lapsed.
  2. Check your assessment notice for the appeal date, and note whether an appeal is pending.
  3. Collect offers in writing, including one as-is cash price, and compare the closing date and who pays which costs.
  4. Pick a closing office early so the PT-61 and the deed are ready.

Cash buyers and financed buyers both ask for permit records and tax information, so having them in hand shortens the wait. A cash buyer can usually work around an open item, while a lender is more likely to require that it be closed first. If you do the repair work yourself before listing, keep the permit, the final inspection result and any certificate together in one folder so you can hand them to a buyer on request.

Frequently asked questions

Does swapping a Roswell water heater need a permit?

Yes. The Building Division puts water heaters under the plumbing and gas codes, so a permit and inspection apply, along with state licensing for any tradesperson.

What if earlier work on my house had no permit?

Ask the Building Division what its record shows for your address before listing. A permit that lapsed less than 180 days ago can be reinstated, and a buyer's lender may want a Certificate of Completion or Occupancy.

How long do I have to appeal a Fulton County assessment?

Forty-five days from the date printed on the notice. File online, in person or by mail; only assessed value can be challenged. A missed deadline forfeits the appeal.

Is Roswell's population growing?

Not by the estimate for July 1, 2025, which shows 91,505 residents, 1.4% below the April 2020 base. The city is still larger than the 88,346 counted in 2010.

Who records the deed after a Roswell sale?

The deed reaches Fulton County's recording office once the transfer tax is paid and a PT-61 is attached. Whoever runs your closing normally handles both.

Sale options for a Warner Robins homeowner in a hurry

Owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or accept an offer from a buyer paying cash who takes the property in its present state. The cash route usually closes soonest. Houston County handles assessment, billing and recording, while the city of Warner Robins bills its own property tax, which means two accounts to settle early.

Many sellers here have military ties, and orders can impose a firm deadline. Robins Air Force Base is a constant presence behind local moves.

  • A listing agent makes sense when the property shows well and time is not tight.
  • Go it alone if you want control over price and showings.
  • Cash fits a short closing, big repairs, or a wish to avoid showings.

On any route, start by collecting your deed, payoff statement and HOA documents.

Selling around a military move

If a reassignment is behind your sale, tell your agent or buyer the report date up front. Military buyers frequently work against a set window, so a seller who can match it stands out. Families moving in from elsewhere also tend to ask about schools first. Warner Robins High School received the Military Flagship School Award from the Georgia Department of Education in 2021, a recognition for schools that support military students and their families, so it is worth a mention in a listing.

Service members get one filing rule worth knowing. Houston County lets someone stationed in Georgia by military order who does not claim Georgia as a residence complete a Service Members Affidavit for Exemption on a boat or aircraft return. Someone stationed here must refile it annually, and business returns are excluded.

Warner Robins housing numbers

Warner Robins counted 66,588 people in 2010 and is estimated at 87,761 for July 1, 2025. The housing and income lines below come from 2020 to 2024 estimates.

Schools and likely buyers

Houston County School System schools serve Warner Robins addresses. The district has 40 schools and over 30,000 students, and Warner Robins High School is one of five high schools. Attendance zones can change over time, so call Houston County Schools to confirm the school assigned to your address before telling a buyer where their children would go.

Expect family buyers. Households average 2.59 persons, and children under 18 are 27.3 percent of residents. They will weigh yard size, bedroom count and the school assignment first.

Anyone who dislikes waiting on a family buyer's loan can look at a cash purchaser, who rents or renovates houses and may close sooner. Either side can search and pay taxes online through the Houston County Tax Commissioner, with a convenience fee, to confirm the account is clear.

Houston County taxes

Houston County assesses real estate at 40 percent of its January 1 market value. Billing is not the assessors' job, so balance questions go to the Tax Commissioner.

Visit the Warner Robins tax office at 202 Carl Vinson Parkway, (478) 542-2110, open weekdays 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. A Perry office handles county business at 201 Perry Parkway, (478) 218-4940. For city bills, call (478) 929-1148, so confirm both accounts before closing.

  • Appeals: a value-change notice starts a 45-day clock, with review by the assessors first and Superior Court as the last step.
  • Grounds: taxability, value or uniformity, and never the size of the bill.
  • Homestead: file the first application by April 1, and it renews on its own until ownership changes.
  • Personal property returns for a business, boat or aircraft are also due April 1.

Each year's tax digest and any tax-increase notice appear on the county site. For real estate valuation questions, call the assessors' Real Estate Department at (478) 218-4750.

Before closing

Look for unpaid taxes on anything tied to the sale and request a payoff for each lien on the title. Houston County assessors warn that buyers of a business, boat or aircraft sometimes find years of unpaid personal property tax afterward, because attorneys usually check only real estate taxes.

Ask the City of Warner Robins code enforcement and building inspection offices whether a violation or open permit is recorded against your address, and resolve anything they show before you list.

If tenants live there, build their move-out or lease assignment into your schedule, because some buyers want an empty house. Clear debris, keep the lawn cut and schedule utility transfers for the closing date.

A simple order of steps

  1. Gather the deed, the payoff statement from your lender and any HOA documents.
  2. Check both tax accounts, county and city, and note any balance. The tax office on Carl Vinson Parkway can tell you what is owed.
  3. Ask the city's code enforcement and building inspection offices whether anything is open against your address.
  4. Decide whether you are listing, selling on your own or asking for cash bids. If a military report date is driving the sale, say so to every buyer.
  5. Accept an offer, open title, and have the closing attorney pay off liens and file the PT-61.
  6. Sign, record the deed with the Clerk of Superior Court, and move utilities into the buyer's name on the closing date.

A cash sale compresses the middle of that list. There is no buyer loan to approve and no lender appraisal to schedule, so the date depends mostly on how fast title work finishes. A financed buyer adds both steps, which is why timing is harder to promise.

If the house needs repairs, decide early whether to fix them yourself or sell as is. Either way, an open permit or code violation can stall any buyer, cash or financed, so clear those first.

Deed recording and transfer tax

Recording happens at the county Clerk of Superior Court, and the transfer tax comes first. The state revenue page prints the rate.

Sellers owe the tax unless the contract says the buyer will pay, and Form PT-61 is e-filed online. Exemption questions go to the clerk. Your closing attorney or title company normally handles the filing and deducts the tax from your proceeds, so ask for the figure in advance.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends property tax bills in Warner Robins?

Both. The Houston County Tax Commissioner handles county billing at (478) 542-2110, and (478) 929-1148 is the number for city billing questions.

How much time do I have to contest a Houston County value change?

Forty-five days from receipt of the notice. File with the county assessors first. If that fails, the Board of Equalization hears it, and Superior Court is the last step.

What is the Houston County homestead filing deadline?

The first year you claim it, April 1. After approval the exemption renews each year unless ownership changes or you apply for a different one.

Can I sell quickly if a military transfer is coming?

Often, yes. Cash buyers can close on the date you name, whereas a financed buyer's loan sets the pace. Give your report date to everyone involved.

The county Clerk of Superior Court, once the transfer tax is paid and the PT-61 is filed.

Most go through a broker listing, some negotiate directly with a buyer, and a smaller group takes an investor's cash bid. The deciding factors are the calendar and the shape of the house. Johns Creek lies in northeastern Fulton County, so the tax bills and recording steps involve Fulton County as well as the city.

A broker listing fits a house that photographs well, since it reaches the biggest group of buyers, at the price of staging, inspections and a lender's appraisal. Negotiating directly saves the commission and hands every task to you. An investor's cash bid gives up price in return for speed and certainty.

  • Highest price: a prepared listing, ideally with a broker who knows your subdivision and school zone.
  • Most control: a direct sale, if contracts and disclosures do not worry you.
  • Fastest or easiest: an investor bid on a house with condition problems.

Whatever you choose, assemble the deed, the newest Fulton County tax bill, any homeowner association papers and the permits for work done on the house. Permit history is easy to retrieve because the city issues permits through an online portal.

Johns Creek housing figures

The 2025 estimate for Johns Creek is 80,401 people, and four of every five homes are lived in by their owners, 80.4 percent for 2020-2024. The midpoint home value is $629,400.

With that many owner-occupied homes, a typical Johns Creek sale is one resident handing a lived-in house to another family. Households average 2.82 people, so the family-sized house is the usual comparison.

Basics buyers ask about

Johns Creek incorporated on December 1, 2006, and covers about 32 square miles roughly 25 miles north of Atlanta. Recreation and Parks maintains more than 400 acres of parkland and nature reserve, with five access points to the Chattahoochee River.

  • Mail can carry a Johns Creek address with any of five ZIP codes: 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 or 30097.
  • The city does not run garbage collection, so residents contract with private haulers.
  • Water comes through Fulton County, and power through Georgia Power or Sawnee Electric.
  • Police and fire service come from the city's own departments.

Have those answers ready. A mailing address can carry a neighboring city's name, so buyers should confirm the property is inside Johns Creek with the city's address tool.
