Schools

Fulton County Schools serves Johns Creek, and 19 of its public elementary, middle and high schools serve residents. Which one a child attends depends on the address and the attendance zone.

Eleven Fulton County elementary schools and one charter school serve the city, with names such as Abbotts Hill, Barnwell, Dolvin, Findley Oaks, Medlock Bridge, Ocee, Shakerag, State Bridge Crossing and Wilson Creek. Some of the elementary schools carry Roswell or Alpharetta mailing addresses even though they serve Johns Creek families. Four private schools also serve the city: Holy Redeemer Catholic School, Mount Pisgah Christian School, Perimeter School and Woodward Academy North.

Zoning is address-specific, so do not tell a buyer which school a house feeds without checking. Direct buyers to Fulton County Schools to confirm the current zone for the exact address.

If you are selling a house that needs work, tell buyers early which repairs you know about.

Where a Johns Creek tax bill comes from

Johns Creek owners owe tax to Fulton County, which includes the school system, and to the City of Johns Creek. The Fulton County Tax Commissioner mails the bill.

The Fulton County Board of Assessors sets the value and mails the Notice of Assessment each year. The notice prints the appeal deadline, so read it as soon as it arrives. Homeowners who qualify for a homestead exemption but miss the April 1 filing date can still apply during the appeal period, and anyone who bought after January 1 applies for the 2027 tax year. Each notice now shows estimated tax savings, with discounts and exemptions, in place of an estimated tax figure.

  • Search your parcel on the Fulton assessor's site to verify the exemptions on record.
  • Ask the Fulton County Tax Commissioner whether the current bill is paid.
  • Have your closing attorney show how this year's tax is shared with the new owner.

Permits and code rules

Johns Creek runs building permits through an online customer self-service portal, and its permit process has six steps: application, fee payment, plan review, permit issued, required inspections and permit completed. The city also posts a Do I Need a Permit checklist.

If you finished a basement, built a deck or replaced a major system without a permit, a buyer's inspection may find it. The city's Code Compliance Division enforces the local ordinances and property maintenance code, and the nuisance and zoning ordinances are posted on its code regulations page. Ask Community Development whether any permit on your address is still open and close it out before you list.

Recording the deed also triggers Georgia's transfer tax. Check the contract to see which side pays.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Johns Creek houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps from accepted offer to closing

After you accept an offer, a title search confirms who owns the house and whether any liens remain. Your closing attorney prepares a settlement statement showing the payoff, the shared tax and any fees. The buyer pays by wire or by lender funding, and the deed is recorded in Fulton County.

With a cash buyer, the lender's appraisal and underwriting drop out of the sequence, which is where most delay comes from in a financed sale. With a financed buyer, expect an inspection and an appraisal, and either can bring a request to lower the price. Keep permit records and receipts for major work in one folder so questions get quick answers.

When an investor's bid makes sense

An investor's bid is worth a look when you cannot or will not prepare the house for retail buyers. Houses here carry high values, and a dated or damaged one can sit while carrying costs keep running.

  • An estate house whose heirs live elsewhere.
  • Deferred maintenance that would not survive a buyer's inspection.
  • A relocation with a short fuse.
  • Past work done without a permit.

Request any bid in writing, see which closing charges are yours, and set it beside a listing broker's net estimate.

Ask each investor how soon they can close, whether an inspection can cancel the deal, and what happens if they back out. A firm answer to those three questions tells you more than the headline price does.

Frequently asked questions

Do Johns Creek owners pay both city and county tax?

Yes. Fulton County, including the school system, and the City of Johns Creek each tax the property, and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner sends the bill.

Is a Johns Creek mailing address always inside the city?

Not always. Johns Creek shares the ZIP codes 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 and 30097 with neighboring cities, and the city offers an address lookup tool for confirmation.

Who hauls trash at a Johns Creek house?

A private company does. The city provides no garbage collection, so residents contract on their own, and a buyer will ask which hauler serves the house.

Can I still file for a Fulton County homestead exemption after April 1?

Owners who qualify but missed April 1 can apply during the appeal period printed on the notice. Anyone who bought after January 1 applies for the 2027 tax year.

Which side pays Georgia's transfer tax on a Johns Creek sale?

State law makes the seller liable, though contracts often move the cost to the buyer. It must be paid before the deed is recorded.

Choosing how to sell in Mableton

Mableton sellers can list with an agent, handle the sale alone, or take an as-is offer. Weigh the cost of repairs against the date you need to move. A listing reaches buyers who rely on mortgages and works best on a house that shows well. A private sale keeps the agent's share but puts pricing, showings and contracts on you. A cash buyer takes the house in its present condition and skips the lender's appraisal.

Get every offer's terms in writing, including who pays the state transfer tax and how the county and city tax bills will be settled at closing.

Market snapshot

Mableton is a south Cobb County community that voted for cityhood on November 8, 2022, and elected its first council on March 21, 2023. The 2025 estimate is 78,820 people, up from 77,077 in April 2020. Of 29,109 households, 64.6 percent own their homes. The median home is worth $313,100, owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,777 a month, and gross rent runs about $1,472.

Nearly nine in ten residents stayed at the same address for a year, so many sellers on established streets have owned for a long time. With this many people and plenty of competing listings, condition and price matter most. Price against what is actually for sale on your street.

Location and neighborhood factors

Mableton lies about 15 miles west-northwest of Atlanta and about 20 miles from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. The Silver Comet Trail, a 61.5-mile paved path that starts in Smyrna, crosses Floyd Road in Mableton, and a buyer who works nearby or toward Smyrna may value that commute more than new finishes.

Fulton County Airport, known as Brown Field, touches Mableton's southeast border. It has two runways and about 65,000 operations a year, so a house on that side may hear aircraft. Expect buyers to ask.

Cobb County's school district runs the public schools. Elementary schools in the area include Mableton, Clay-Harmony Leland, Bryant, Riverside, Russell and City View. Pebblebrook and South Cobb are the high schools. Assignment follows the address, so check it with the district before you name a school in your listing.

New development nearby

County planning documents describe a Mableton Town Center vision for the Mableton Parkway area, approved by the Cobb Board of Commissioners in 2013. Later projects include a 31-acre mixed-use plaza near Mableton Parkway and Old Powder Springs Road with townhomes, courtyard cottages and detached houses, and a 60-acre redevelopment along Floyd Road with apartments and townhomes, approved on October 21, 2020.

New construction nearby can raise buyer interest in the area, and it also gives buyers newer alternatives. Treat it as a reason to price carefully, not as a selling point you can quantify.

Who bills what: Cobb County and the city

The city has no general property tax. Cobb County keeps billing county and school taxes, and Mableton sends separate bills for its special service districts. The county assessor values property at 40 percent of market and mails notices in early summer. Cobb bills go out in August and are due October 15.

The city's Public Safety Special Services District covers police services the city took over from Cobb on June 1, 2025. The city began billing it in October 2026 at 4.5 mills, applied to the assessed value set by Cobb. A separate Six Flags Special Services District has been billed by the city since October 2025.

Handling both bills at closing

The city applies its millage to the assessed value Cobb sets. Ask the city finance office for the district bill's due date, and keep proof of payment for the closing file. The state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant appears as a separate reduction on eligible Cobb bills, and anyone who loses homestead eligibility must tell the Tax Commissioner.

Homestead exemption after a sale

The homestead exemption is a break for owners who live in the house as a primary residence. Cobb's assessor sets a filing deadline each July. An owner who is no longer eligible must report it before the appeal deadline or owe the back taxes and interest, plus a 50 percent penalty on the amount wrongly reduced.

After a sale, make sure the Tax Commissioner and your closing attorney know the house stopped being your primary residence at transfer.

Permits and building rules

Mableton's Building Division reviews plans against Georgia's minimum standard codes, inspects work and issues Certificates of Occupancy. Applications go through the online CloudPermit portal only, and emailed ones are refused. Crews may work 7 AM to 7 PM weekdays and 9 AM to 5 PM Saturdays, never on Sundays or designated holidays.

  • Collect permits and final inspection records for recent work.
  • Ask the general contractor to confirm each inspection passed.
  • If the home was rented, ask the city's Business License office whether any registration is still active.

A house in poor repair can still be sold as is, to a buyer who accepts the condition. Keep permit records for earlier work so title review does not stall the closing.

Georgia deed transfer tax

The state's transfer tax is printed as $1 for the first $1,000 of price, or fractional part of $1,000, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. Your contract may shift it to the buyer. Either way, the deed cannot be recorded with the court clerk until the tax is paid.

Paperwork to have ready

  1. The deed and your mortgage payoff details.
  2. The latest Cobb tax bill and any city district bill.
  3. Permit and final inspection records for recent work.
  4. Any notice about a pending value appeal, because it changes the bill a buyer will see.

With these in one folder, an agent can answer a buyer's questions the same day, and a cash buyer can make a firm offer without waiting on records. A sale that runs through a lender also moves faster when the tax bills and permit history are already in hand, since the title company asks for them early.

Talk to the closing attorney before you sign, so the contract says plainly who is responsible for each charge that falls between the first of January and the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

Does Mableton levy a city property tax?

There is no general city levy. Mableton bills a Public Safety district at 4.5 mills, which began in October 2026, and a Six Flags district it has billed since October 2025. Cobb still bills county and school taxes.

When are Cobb property taxes due for Mableton owners?

October 15 each year. The payment must reach the Tax Commissioner's Office or be postmarked by USPS that day.

How long can I contest my Cobb value?

Forty-five days from the date printed on the Notice of Assessment. A parcel with an appeal pending receives a temporary bill at 85 percent of assessed value until it is settled.

Who sets property values inside Mableton?

Cobb County. Values come from the Cobb assessor, and appeals go to the Cobb Board of Tax Assessors, which also oversees homestead filings.

Can a Mableton house in poor repair be sold?

Yes, as is, to a buyer who accepts the condition, or after fixes through a listing. Keep permit records for earlier work so title review does not stall the closing.

Alpharetta lies in the northern part of Fulton County, about 26 miles up from downtown Atlanta. The city spans 26.9 square miles of land, with Johns Creek, Roswell and Milton as neighbors and unincorporated Forsyth County to the northeast.

Corporate offices bring a steady flow of buyers, among them Fiserv, ADP, MCI (Verizon) and Equifax. Downtown, the Avalon district and the Alpha Loop trail system add walkable shopping and recreation that buyers ask about.

Is the address inside Alpharetta city limits?

An Alpharetta mailing address does not guarantee the property lies inside the city. The Halcyon mixed-use district has an Alpharetta postal address yet sits in Forsyth County, outside both the city limits and Fulton County.

That changes who bills the property. The City of Alpharetta levies its own ad valorem tax for city operations and voter-approved bonds and keeps its own homestead exemption page, while Fulton County sets the assessment. A parcel in a neighboring jurisdiction owes tax to different governments. Read your tax bill, or ask the county assessors which governments tax the parcel, before you tell a buyer what the house costs to carry.

School assignment is the other point to confirm. Fulton County Schools serves the city, and Alpharetta High School serves most of it, but the zone depends on the address. Confirm the attendance zone with the school district before putting a school name in your listing.

How to appeal a Fulton County assessment

Fulton sends each property a yearly notice of assessment, and owners who dispute the fair market value it states get 45 days from the notice date to respond. Only the value is open to appeal, and the right ends after the deadline printed on the notice.

  • Filing is online, by mail, or in person at five county sites, one of them the North Fulton center at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210.
  • The form asks you to pick a hearing path, and arbitration or a hearing officer can add fees.
  • Review can take months, and a temporary bill that arrives meanwhile still has to be paid.

Mention an unresolved appeal to your closing attorney before the settlement date.

City services and permits when selling

The city's Apply menu gathers the forms a seller may need: a permitting portal, building construction permits, business licenses, homestead exemptions, and a form to establish or end trash service. Water and sewer bills are paid to Fulton County, so closing that account is a separate step from ending city trash service.

The city also keeps a Short-Term Rentals page under its Business section. If you plan to tell a buyer the house can host nightly guests, get the current rules from the city's planning and zoning staff in writing first. Before closing, look up any deck, finished basement or HVAC replacement in the permitting portal so an unfinished permit does not hold things up.

Ask the city's building permit staff through the portal what is open on the address, and tell the buyer about any permit that has not been finished and approved.

Deed transfer tax at an Alpharetta closing

The transfer tax is an excise on the sale itself, separate from the yearly property tax, and the clerk will not record the deed until it is settled. Alpharetta deeds are recorded in Fulton County, and the state clerks' authority supplies the PT-61 form that reports the sale.

The seller owes it by default. For questions on whether a gift, family or trust transfer is taxable, the revenue department points owners to the county clerk, so call that office before closing.

When a cash sale fits in Alpharetta

At these prices, a listing can pay well, but it also asks a lot of the seller: repairs, staging, showings and a buyer's financing. Cash appeals when one of those becomes a problem.

  • A probate or inherited house that no one wants to update or hold.
  • A relocation with little lead time before a job start.
  • A house needing big updates, where repair quotes cut deep into the sale price.
  • A parcel with an open permit, an unresolved appeal or a tax question that would slow a lender's underwriting.

Compare a cash offer with the likely listing price, then subtract repairs, carrying costs and months on the market. The better route is the one that leaves more in your pocket at closing.

What to bring to your closing attorney

A short folder saves days of back and forth. Bring your deed, your latest Fulton assessment notice, and your tax bill so the attorney can see which governments tax the parcel. If an appeal is still open, say so before the settlement date, since a temporary bill still has to be paid.

Add any permit paperwork for work done since you bought, plus the account details for city trash service and Fulton County water and sewer, so each can be closed or transferred. Ask the attorney who files the PT-61 form and how the transfer tax will appear on the statement. If you plan to sell by cash, the same folder lets the buyer's title company move quickly, and the closing date can be set around your move rather than a lender's timeline. Ask for the payoff on any lien or open tax balance at the same time, so the title search turns up no surprises and the statement is ready when you sign it.

Frequently asked questions

What is a typical Alpharetta home worth?

The Census figure for 2020-2024 is $649,000 for a typical owner-occupied home. Condition and timing can move your own price well above or below it.

What is the cutoff for a Fulton appeal on Alpharetta property?

Fulton allows 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. The date printed on your notice controls, and the appeal covers value only.

Does a 30004 or 30005 mailing address prove the house is in the city?

No. Halcyon, for instance, uses an Alpharetta address but sits in Forsyth County. Check your tax bill or ask the Fulton County Board of Assessors.

Who carries the transfer tax in an Alpharetta contract?

The seller by default, though a contract clause can hand the cost to the buyer. Ask your closing attorney to confirm the amount before the settlement date.

What should I do about an unfinished permit before selling?

Ask the city's building permit staff through the permitting portal what is open on the address, and tell the buyer about any permit that has not been finished and approved.

Three routes come up most among Albany sellers: handing the house to an agent, running the sale yourself, or letting a cash buyer take it in whatever condition it is in. Repair needs, the closing date you require and a location near the river usually decide which path fits.

Flood history and buyer questions

Buyers and their lenders know the Flint River's history. The river flooded badly in 1841 and 1925, and rain from Tropical Storm Alberto in 1994 produced a flood that killed 14 people and displaced 22,000. New homes went up on the south side of town afterward to replace what the water ruined.

If your house is on the older south side or close to the water, expect to be asked whether it ever took in water. Albany's residential inspection guide calls for elevation documentation, sealed by a registered design professional, when building in a flood hazard area. Gather any elevation certificate, flood insurance papers and repair receipts before a buyer asks.

Humid weather and heavy rain also wear on roofs, gutters and crawl-space drainage, so a buyer's inspector will look at those areas first and may ask for credits.

What Dougherty County's 2026 revaluation changed

The county sent 2026 assessment notices after completing its first countywide revaluation in more than 10 years, so many values moved up to match current prices. The notice lists assessed value only. The bill follows once the appeal period closes, the digest is final, and the commissioners adopt a millage rate.

  • The 45-day appeal clock starts on the mailing date.
  • Senate Bill 581 set up the statewide floating homestead exemption, which can hold down growth in the taxable value of a qualifying home.
  • Senate Bill 566 redesigned the notice to show the deadline and estimated savings.

Acreage at the city's edge may carry an agricultural or conservation classification. Those applications are filed between January 1 and April 1, cost $25, and bind the owner to the qualifying use for 10 years. If your land is enrolled, phone the Board of Assessors before signing a contract so a change in use does not surprise either side.

Permits before fixing up an Albany house

Permitted work follows a fixed inspection order, and a skipped step can stall a sale. The city's Planning and Development Services guide says the permit stays on site until the job ends and approved plans must be present at every inspection.

The order is foundation, rough plumbing, mechanical, gas and electrical, framing and masonry, then a final inspection before anyone occupies the work. A request in by 4:00 p.m. is scheduled for the next business day, and the city may charge for a re-inspection when work is unready or fails twice.

Someone paying cash accepts the house as is, which lets an owner who dislikes juggling contractors sidestep the whole sequence. If you do plan repairs before listing, ask Planning and Development Services whether a roof, panel, plumbing or HVAC change needs a permit.

Deed and transfer tax at closing

Georgia taxes the transfer, and nothing gets recorded until that is paid. The schedule is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part.

By default the bill falls on the seller, and a contract clause can move it to the buyer. Form PT-61 is submitted electronically through the clerks' cooperative authority (GSCCCA), and the Dougherty County superior court clerk records the deed itself. Ask your settlement attorney how the year's property tax will be divided on the statement.

When a fast as-is sale makes sense

Several local circumstances push owners toward a quick sale.

  • A south-side or river-area house that came through an estate, needs work and has back taxes.
  • A rental where the tenant stopped paying, or one that sits empty and costs more than it earns.
  • A home with storm, roof or water damage where repair quotes run higher than you want to spend.
  • A property with liens or overdue taxes that you want cleared at the closing table.

Line up a cash price against the likely listing price, take out repair bills, carrying costs and months on the market, and compare what each route leaves in your pocket.

How a cash sale works, step by step

The process is shorter than a listing because no lender is involved. You describe the house and its condition, including any tenant, back taxes or storm damage. The buyer makes an offer based on what you describe. If you accept, a closing attorney or title company searches the title, finds any lien or tax balance, and prepares the settlement statement.

Gather what the attorney will ask for: the deed, any lease, flood or elevation papers, and a recent tax bill. On the closing day you sign, the transfer tax is paid so the deed can be recorded, and any payoff comes out of your proceeds. You pick the closing date within reason, which helps if you are moving, settling an estate or ending a lease. Because the house sells as is, you skip repairs, showings and the wait for a buyer's financing. If a tenant lives there, say so up front, since the lease terms decide whether the closing waits or the tenant stays in place. If the house sits near the river, bring any flood insurance papers so the buyer and the title company are not surprised later in the process.

Frequently asked questions

Can a flood-damaged Albany house still be sold?

Yes. Buyers who pay cash take storm and water damage as part of the deal. Keep photos, insurance claim papers and any elevation certificate, since a lender may ask about flood hazard status.

Who owes the transfer tax in an Albany deal?

The seller, unless the sales contract assigns it to the buyer. The amount follows the state schedule.

What is the window to contest a Dougherty County value?

Owners get 45 days, counted from the day the county mails the notice. The Board of Assessors reviews the appeal.

Must an Albany rental be empty before closing?

No. A tenant does not block a sale; the house can change hands with the lease running or after it expires. Check the lease for notice and entry terms before showings.

Where does the Albany deed get recorded?

At the Dougherty County superior court clerk's office after the tax is paid and form PT-61 is in. Ask your closing attorney which party files it.

Three ways to sell a Marietta house

Your options in Marietta: hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or accept a cash offer. Repairs and timing usually point to one of them.

Hiring an agent brings in mortgage buyers, and with them showings, inspection requests and a closing date that follows the lender. Doing it yourself saves the agent's share but hands you pricing, marketing and negotiation. A cash buyer closes sooner and asks for no repair list, but the price reflects the house as it stands today.

Typical home values here are $448,500, so a small percentage gap between two offers is a big gap in cash. Compare terms in writing before you decide, and ask each buyer who pays closing costs and when funds arrive.

Marietta housing snapshot

About 63,574 people live in Marietta today by the 2025 estimate, up 4.1% from the 61,060 used as the 2020 starting point. Renters fill just over half the homes, since owners occupy 47.2%. Owner costs are $2,170 a month with a mortgage and $618 without. Gross rent is $1,586. The city has 24,707 households averaging 2.40 people.

Owners of older houses near the Square should ask the city which exterior changes need approval in the historic district before promising a buyer any work. Code Enforcement covers that district along with zoning and signs.

Building and code rules

The City of Marietta enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building Code and International Residential Code, with 2026 Georgia amendments, for projects permitted after January 1, 2026. Plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes follow the 2024 editions as well, and the electrical code is the 2023 National Electrical Code with 2026 Georgia amendments.

All building permits are submitted online. Pulling a permit before repairs matters at sale time, because a buyer's inspector or title review may turn up unpermitted work. The Building Inspection Division answers questions at 770-794-5659.

Code Enforcement checks building code, zoning, signs, the historic district and the standard housing code. It sits at 205 Lawrence Street, phone 770-794-5439, and it can act only on properties inside the city limits. Cobb County property tax and Marietta's city bill

County and school taxes both come on a bill from Cobb's Tax Commissioner. The seven cities inside Cobb, Marietta among them, run their own billing, so ask the City of Marietta about its separate portion.

The county does not split the bill between seller and buyer. Who owes what is set by the closing paperwork, and the purchaser generally takes on the liability. The tax is figured for the full year and follows the property.

Paying the bill

Partial payments are fine, and a postmark from the U.S. Post Office dated by midnight on the deadline counts as on time. Metered or kiosk postage does not count. An owner appealing a value must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date. Pay at 736 Whitlock Avenue, Suite 100, Marietta, or by mail to PO Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061. Drop boxes sit outside the Whitlock Avenue office, and the East Cobb and South Cobb Government Service Centers take payments too.

Buyers can try the Tax Commissioner's estimator for new home purchasers: enter a fair market value, choose the city or unincorporated tax district and select exemptions. A seller can run it to show a buyer roughly what the county side of the bill will be.

Selling with unpaid Cobb taxes

After the last day for payment, Cobb sends the taxpayer a written notice. If thirty days go by unpaid, a fi. fa. (an execution) can be issued under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3. The debt follows the house, so clear any balance well before closing.

Tax sales run on the first Tuesday of each month in which a sale is planned, held on the Superior Courthouse steps at Flournoy Park in Marietta between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Cobb publishes a Tax Sale Booklet on the process. Your deed gets recorded by the Cobb clerk only once the state transfer tax is paid and a PT-61 is on file. Your own homestead exemption ends at the sale, and Cobb asks owners who sold or moved to say so, since staying silent can bring a penalty. The new owner will need the recorded deed to reapply for an exemption of their own.

From signed contract to closing day

With a contract signed, paperwork takes over. The closing attorney or title company pulls the Cobb bill, asks the city for its share and checks that no execution was filed against the parcel. Because the county tax is figured for the full year and follows the property, the settlement statement should show clearly who covers which stretch of the year.

If you are selling to a cash buyer, the same steps apply, only faster, because no lender is waiting on an appraisal. If you appeal a value while a sale is pending, remember that you must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date.

Getting ready to list

Before listing, round up the deed, a mortgage payoff figure, current Cobb and city tax bills and permit records for repairs. Check the property search to learn whether the city or the county rules apply. A cash buyer will look at the same papers, though the buyer's price will reflect the house as it stands. A listing buyer's lender will want a clean title and settled tax bills, so clear any balance before an offer comes in. If a tenant lives there, say so up front and plan around the notice the lease requires.

Frequently asked questions

Who covers Cobb property tax when a Marietta house closes?

The contract and settlement statement decide. The Tax Commissioner does not prorate between the parties, and liability generally passes to the purchaser.

What is the payment deadline on a Cobb tax bill?

Bills go out by August 15 and are due October 15. A 5% penalty follows, with interest added monthly. The city bill is separate, so ask Marietta for its date.

Can I get a Marietta building permit online?

Yes. The city takes all permits online, and its Building Inspection Division at 770-794-5659 can answer questions. Code Enforcement at 770-794-5439 handles complaints inside city limits only.

Is every Marietta mailing address inside city limits?

Not always. A Marietta mailing address does not place a property inside the limits. The city's Property Search Tool shows which government's rules apply.

What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?

It stops when you sell. Let the Tax Commissioner know you no longer qualify, and expect the buyer to file a new application on their own.

Your options for selling in Stonecrest

Sellers in this city end up choosing between a listing agent, a do-it-yourself sale, and a quick cash purchase where the investor deals with repairs. The right pick follows the condition of the roof and kitchen, your loan payoff, your moving date, and who is living there now.

  • A listing agent fits a tidy house and an owner with time to wait.
  • Going solo saves the commission, though you take on pricing, disclosure forms and haggling.
  • Ask for cash bids if the house has deferred repairs, tax arrears or a probate matter hanging over it.

Stonecrest sits inside DeKalb County, so county offices handle property tax on every parcel, while the city keeps its own permit and business license staff. Knowing who answers what saves phone calls later.

Stonecrest at a glance

The city is young. Incorporation passed by vote on November 8, 2016, and the city began operating on July 10, 2017. Its own staff cover zoning, code enforcement, business licenses and building permits. The county still provides police, fire, road upkeep and sanitation. The city set its first millage rate in 2020, so ask the DeKalb Tax Commissioner what city levy, if any, appears on your bill.

The estimated population is 61,337, in 20,995 households, and owners occupy 56.3 percent of the homes. With nearly half the homes rented, investors planning a rental belong in your buyer pool.

What buyers like about the area

Retail in the city centers on the Mall at Stonecrest, ringed by medical, office and hotel parcels around it and DeKalb Medical Center at Hillandale as the main hospital. Interstate 20 and State Routes 124 and 278 lead toward downtown Atlanta and Hartsfield-Jackson airport. Two industrial areas hold some of the larger local employers, so a buyer who works at one of them may want a short drive.

Outdoor space is the other draw. The Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area covers 2,550 acres of exposed granite, wetlands, streams, lakes and forest linked by trails, and Davidson-Arabia Mountain Nature Park and Panola Mountain State Park sit nearby. A listing or a cash pitch can mention the drive to the mall corridor or the trailheads, since those are the things people ask about first.

Due dates and penalties

The August mailing is addressed to the January 1 titleholder, and a second copy goes to a newer owner if there is one. Choose between two payments (September 30 and November 15) or one payment by September 30. For mailed payments, a clerk's hand-canceled postmark dated by the deadline is the proof the county accepts. A meter stamp or kiosk label will not count. Miss the date and the penalty is 5 percent.

The county does not mail bills to lenders. Owners with escrow should ask the servicer to confirm the payment went out before listing.

On a single-family home, the county prints a yearly sanitation assessment for trash pickup of $362.30 on the same bill.

Who pays at closing

For a sale that closes after January 1, the county's advice to the buyer is to read the closing statement or ask the attorney, lender or escrow agent who owes the bill. Any balance remains a charge on the land itself. Request an itemized tax line on the settlement statement so both sides see the split.

Overdue taxes get paid from your sale proceeds at the closing table. Cash buyers rarely balk at this, which is why owners behind on taxes often start with cash bids.

Homestead exemption and appeals

DeKalb's homestead test asks three things: the house is your main residence on January 1, your Georgia license or ID shows that address, and your vehicles are registered there. Filing closes in mid-July. An exemption is never granted on its own and does not move to the buyer, who must file a fresh application. Once granted, an exemption puts an assessment freeze on county taxes that may limit increases, though it does not touch school, city or state taxes.

  • Special exemptions with income limits exist for homeowners 62 and older, disabled homeowners, former service members rated 100 percent disabled, and some surviving spouses.
  • From the date of the notice you have 45 days to appeal. Fax and email filings get rejected, so deliver it by hand or mail.
  • You can take the case to the Board of Equalization (free), to nonbinding arbitration ($217 plus a certified appraisal), or, for non-homestead property valued over $500,000, to a hearing officer.
  • An appeal still open when bills print means you pay on a temporary value, typically the lower of last year's final figure or 85 percent of this year's.

The county appraises at 100 percent of market value and taxes 40 percent of that. The Property Appraisal Department is at 325 Swanton Way in Decatur, and the Tax Commissioner's central office is at 4380 Memorial Drive in Decatur.

Before you call the county

Have the parcel number and the property address ready, plus your most recent assessment notice if you have one. The Property Appraisal Department answers value questions, and the Tax Commissioner's office answers billing and payment questions. Keeping those two straight shortens most calls. If you plan to dispute a value, start counting the 45 days from the date on the notice, not from the day it reaches your mailbox.

Transfer tax and recording

Georgia's recording rule is simple: no transfer tax, no recorded deed. Sellers carry the cost unless the contract moves it. The rate is posted on the Department of Revenue's transfer tax page, and the PT-61 declaration goes in electronically from you or your closing office.

If you doubt that your transfer is taxable, the Clerk of Superior Court in the county can answer. Most closing attorneys file the form and subtract the tax from what you receive.

Checklist before you accept an offer

  1. Pull together your deed, DeKalb parcel number and latest assessment notice.
  2. Find out if a homestead exemption is on file and tell buyers it ends when you sell.
  3. Open the August bill and mark which installments you have paid.
  4. Order a payoff statement from your lender and a lien search through the closing attorney.
  5. Weigh each offer by the net you walk away with after transfer tax, repair credits and the closing date.

With cash there is no buyer mortgage and no lender appraisal, so two usual causes of delay disappear. The price is often lower in exchange, so keep two or three bids in front of you.

Frequently asked questions

Is Stonecrest its own city?

Yes. Voters created it on November 8, 2016, and it began operating on July 10, 2017. The city runs zoning, permits and business licenses, while DeKalb County bills property tax and handles public safety.

When are DeKalb County property tax installments due?

Two payments are due, September 30 and November 15. A single full payment must be in by September 30. Late payments carry a 5 percent penalty, and the postmark rules are strict.

Does my DeKalb homestead exemption go to the buyer?

No. It stays with you. The buyer files a new application and has to meet the January 1 ownership and residency tests.

What is the DeKalb appeal deadline?

The limit is 45 days from the date the notice was mailed. Hand-deliver the appeal or mail it so it is postmarked in time, since fax and email filings are refused.

Who pays the tax bill after I sell?

Your closing statement should say. DeKalb sends one bill to the January 1 owner and another to the new owner, and it points buyers to the closing attorney or escrow agent for the answer. Any unpaid amount remains with the property.

Which sale route is fastest in Brookhaven

Pace varies by route. An as-is buyer with cash can set the closing day with you, whereas a listing waits on showings, an appraisal and the buyer's mortgage. The money at stake is large. The 2020 to 2024 midpoint for a Brookhaven owner-occupied house is $692,700, about twice the $332,700 U.S. figure, so one percentage point of price is a lot of dollars.

  • Full listing: strongest exposure, plus staging, repair lists and the lender's calendar.
  • Owner-handled sale: no commission to pay, but buyers, contracts and disclosures are yours to manage.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer steps and no repair demands, normally at a figure below a polished listing.

The sections below cover what is particular to Brookhaven: housing numbers, permit rules, code enforcement and the DeKalb County tax process.

A young city in DeKalb County

Brookhaven incorporated in December 2012, and its police department opened for service on July 31, 2013. It covers 11.69 square miles of land and runs 19 parks, three swimming pools, two recreation centers and a community building on 352 acres of parkland.

Water and sewer come from DeKalb County, and DeKalb's watershed department staffs a 24-hour emergency line at 770-270-6243. Rules on short-term rentals, building permits and construction hours come from the city's own code, so check Brookhaven's pages, not the county's, when you plan work on a house here.

Brookhaven housing numbers

Brookhaven had 59,643 residents in mid-2025, 5.1 percent above the April 2020 estimates base, living in 24,271 households that average 2.36 people.

Brookhaven housing and income, 2020 to 2024 survey period
Housing measureBrookhaven
Owner-occupied share of homes52.6%

Every figure covers the whole city, so one house may sit far off the midpoint. Buyers and tenants here come from a wide mix of backgrounds, and a listing with clear photos and plain, specific details reaches all of them.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Brookhaven house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Short-term rental permits

Brookhaven allows short-term rentals only for a resident owner holding a permit. Council adopted the Short-Term Rental Ordinance on April 23, 2019, and each permitted house may be rented no more than 180 days per year.

  • The applicant must have owned the property for over a year and hold a current DeKalb homestead exemption.
  • No permit goes to a business entity such as an LLC, a partnership or a family trust.
  • One owner, one permit, and permits are limited to five percent of residential parcels in each council district.
  • The permit costs $25 for one year and renews annually.

The permit ends when the property changes hands, so a buyer who wants a rental starts a fresh application. For permits that predate October 24, 2023, a new owner has six months after title transfer to apply without being turned away on the district cap. Ask Community Development how your council district stands before you pitch the house to investors.

Permits and work hours when preparing to sell

Construction or redevelopment of any kind needs a city permit from the Community Development Department. Contractors present a Georgia license, while a homeowner working on their own house can sign a notarized Homeowner Affidavit.

Wait 10 business days for review before calling about status. The city's fee schedule lists the minimum and review fees, which use the ICC data valuation table. Complaints about work outside permitted hours go to police through 911. Allowed hours are 7 am to 7 pm Monday to Friday and 8 am to 5 pm on Saturday, with no work on Sunday. You can also report construction without a permit, and tree removal without one, through the Brookhaven Connect app. Close out permits on finished work before a buyer's inspector asks about it.

DeKalb assessments and appeals

DeKalb County, not the city, appraises Brookhaven homes. Its appraisal department sets taxable value at fair market value times 40 percent. If you dispute the value, the recorded property features or a homestead denial, you have 45 days from the notice date to appeal.

Three appeal paths exist. The Board of Equalization costs nothing and uses a three-member panel. A hearing officer is available at no filing fee for non-homestead property over $500,000. Non-binding arbitration needs a certified appraisal at the owner's expense and a $217 filing fee. File online with the access code printed on the notice, or mail the appeal to 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Brookhaven houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption filing dates

The share of the DeKalb homestead exemption you receive depends on when you file.

  • January 1 to April 1: 100.00% of the exemption.
  • April 2 to April 30: 66.67%.
  • May 1 to May 31: 58.33%.
  • June 1 to June 30: 50.00%.

Ask the DeKalb tax commissioner what remains due on the current bill so the amount can be divided at closing. A buyer who sees a reduced exemption on the bill will ask why, and the filing date is usually the answer. If you are selling soon after buying, check that your own application went in before April 2.

Code enforcement before you list

Neighbors can report problems through the Brookhaven Connect app, and the list reads like a pre-listing checklist: tall grass or vegetation, trash or outside storage, inoperable vehicles, illegal dumping, graffiti, construction without a permit and tree removal without a permit. A house with an open complaint can slow a buyer's lender or surprise a cash buyer, so walk the lot and clear these items first.

Police dispatch runs through ChatComm, so 911 doubles as the non-emergency line. The city's parcel and land-use maps can help you check zoning and boundaries before you list. Ask Community Development about any open permit or violation on your address. Unresolved items are far easier to clear before a contract than after. A cash buyer will often take a house with a few open items, but the price will reflect the work, so a clean record helps in either kind of sale.

Reporting and recording the sale

DeKalb County will not record your deed until Georgia's transfer tax is settled. The sale is reported on Form PT-61, filed electronically through the clerks' portal. The tax is $1 up to the first $1,000 of price, then 10 cents for every additional $100 or part of $100, and the seller is liable unless the contract says differently.

For a ruling on whether a particular deed is exempt, ask the county clerk. Filing trouble goes to the portal's support line at 800-304-5174, and whoever runs your closing normally files the form.

Is Brookhaven a long-established city?

What is the midpoint home value in Brookhaven?

Will a new buyer inherit my short-term rental permit?

No. The permit ends when ownership changes. Permits go only to owner-occupants with a DeKalb homestead exemption who have owned the property for more than a year.

What is the deadline to dispute a DeKalb value?

Forty-five days from the notice date. Use the access code on the notice to file online, or mail the appeal to DeKalb County Property Appraisal, 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

Who pays Georgia's transfer tax at a Brookhaven closing?

The seller, by default, and a contract can move it to the buyer. It is paid ahead of recording, with PT-61 filed online.

Selling in Smyrna

Smyrna is a compact Cobb County city of 15.4 square miles, sixteen miles out from downtown Atlanta, just west of where I-285 meets I-75 at Cumberland. Smyrna had 55,663 residents in 24,600 households at the 2020 count. Redevelopment since the early 1990s swapped townhouses and condominiums in for older neighborhoods, so look at what homes on your own block sold for lately.

One difference from most Georgia cities: Smyrna mails a property tax bill of its own, on top of the county's. Cobb Parkway (U.S. 41), Atlanta Road, South Cobb Drive (State Route 280) and I-285 pass through, and both CobbLinc and MARTA buses stop here. Buyers who commute to Cumberland, the Cobb Galleria or Midtown will care about the minutes each trip takes, so give honest times.

The terrain is typical Georgia Piedmont, with hills, broad ridges and narrow valleys. Buyers will ask about grading, drainage or retaining walls on the lot, so know what was done. The Cobb County School District runs the public schools; zones change from street to street, so send buyers to the district's address lookup.

Smyrna building permits and fees

Permit applications, building or standalone, are filed on the city's online portal. Counter submittals are no longer taken. Permits are good for six months if no activity occurs. Community Development lists these building permit charges:

FeeAmount
Building or land disturbance permit$7 per $1,000 of estimated construction cost
Records fee10 percent of the building permit fee
Standalone or MEP permit$50
Technology fee$15
Minimum building permit$125
Reinspection$50, then $100, $150 and $200 for the fourth and later

Permit and water connection fees can be reduced or waived for projects approved under the city's development incentive program. If you cannot tell which line fits your repair, phone the building division before the work begins.

An open or expired permit can surface when a buyer's inspector or a title company checks the address. Permits lapse after six months of no activity, so a repair you started and left half finished is worth looking into. Closing a permit out cleanly before you list removes one reason for a buyer to ask for a lower price. The building division is the office to ask, and it can tell you which permits it holds on file for your parcel. Do this before listing, not after a contract is signed, so any surprise is yours to fix on your own schedule.

Can I sell a Smyrna house that had short-term renters?

Yes, but tidy up the license record first. A short-term rental inside city limits must hold a Short-Term Rental License and an Occupational Tax Certificate, both applied for online. The application asks for:

  • Proof of liability insurance
  • A code compliance verification form
  • A short-term rental agent form
  • Proof of ownership
  • For owner-occupied houses, a homestead exemption or an affidavit in lieu of one

Call the Business License Coordinator at 678-631-5363 and ask if a license transfers to a buyer or has to be reissued. A rental that ran unlicensed should be straightened out with the city before you list, since a buyer's attorney can search for open compliance matters.

How Smyrna city taxes and Cobb County taxes fit together

Smyrna homeowners get two bills, one from Cobb County and one from the city. Cobb assessors set the value, and Georgia taxes 40 percent of it. Assessment notices arrive in early summer with a 45-day appeal period. County bills follow in late summer and are due in the fall.

The city bills separately, in September with payment due in November. Exemptions available through the city include $10,000 for owners aged 62 or over, $22,000 for owners with a 100 percent disability and limited income, and a homestead exemption that caps the city tax at the home's initial assessed value. File city exemption paperwork by April 1 at City Hall, 2800 King Street SE.

Unpaid city taxes lead the city to record a FIFA lien with the Cobb Superior Court clerk, letting it collect before the house can be sold. The county commissioner splits nothing between seller and buyer; liability is fixed at closing, so your contract and settlement statement assign each share.

Owing taxes and moving a deed

Partial payments are accepted by Cobb's tax commissioner. Past the due date, county taxes pick up a 5 percent penalty and monthly interest. An owner with an appeal pending still owes at least the appealed amount on time to dodge the penalty.

The county office describes four common deed types: a recorded warranty deed, a quitclaim deed, a deed of assent used for inherited property, and an executor's deed. Each is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. For an inherited house or a transfer inside the family, an attorney should pick the form.

Georgia's transfer tax falls on the seller unless the contract moves it, charged at $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100.

Owners with a tight deadline can weigh a standard listing against an as-is investor offer or a direct cash sale. Line up what each would put in your pocket once the bills and payoffs are settled.

Choosing a sale route in Smyrna

Three roads lead out: an agent's listing, an as-is investor sale, or a straight cash sale. Listing tends to earn the most on a house in good order, at the price of showings, inspection rounds and a lender's schedule. Selling for cash trades a lower price for a fixed closing date, handy with deferred repairs, a tenant or tax arrears.

With two tax bills in play, ask every buyer's offer to be netted against both. An unpaid city bill can become a lien, and liens must be cleared before a clean deed passes. Have your closing attorney search for liens early, and get a draft settlement statement several days ahead to read the tax lines and payoff.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Smyrna houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Checklist before you accept an offer

  1. Pull the city and county tax bills and mark which are paid.
  2. If you hosted short-term guests, make sure the license and tax records are in order.
  3. Ask building staff to confirm that repairs you made were permitted.
  4. Write into the contract who pays the transfer tax and how taxes are divided at closing.
  5. Hold an as-is cash price up against what a listing would net.
  6. For an inherited house, an attorney should choose the deed form before anything is signed.

Both cash buyers and financed buyers want tax and permit records. Having them early shortens the wait from offer to closing.

Keep a simple folder for the sale. Put the deed, both tax bills, any permit receipts and the rental license papers in it. When a buyer's attorney or a title company asks a question, you can answer in a day instead of hunting through drawers, and a quick answer keeps a good offer from cooling off.

Frequently asked questions

Does the City of Smyrna bill its own property tax?

Yes. Its finance department mails a separate bill in September, due in November, on top of the Cobb County one.

How long do I have to appeal my Cobb County value?

Forty-five days, counted from the date on your assessment notice.

Do I need a license for a short-term rental in Smyrna?

Yes, plus an Occupational Tax Certificate. Applicants provide proof of liability insurance, an agent form and proof of ownership.

What is the cost of a building permit in Smyrna?

Building permits run $7 per $1,000 of estimated construction cost, with a minimum of $125. Technology, records and reinspection fees come on top.

Does the county prorate taxes at closing?

No. Cobb's tax commissioner leaves the split to you, so your sales contract and settlement statement settle who pays.

The fastest way to sell in Valdosta

A cash buyer is usually the quickest route, a sale by owner comes next, and an agent listing takes longest. Demand here is tied to the university, the air base and the regional hospital, so a well-priced house in good condition can also sell through an agent.

The pace is really set by whatever stands between you and a clean closing. In Valdosta that is often an open permit, an overgrown lot that drew a city notice, a back-tax balance or a tenant.

  • Cash buyer: no loan approval, buys as-is, closes when you say.
  • Agent listing: more eyes on the house, plus showings and inspection requests.
  • Owner sale: you write the terms and handle the contract.

Whichever you pick, request a copy of your deed from the Clerk of Superior Court at the Lowndes County Courthouse, 100 Central Street, where county property records are kept.

Who creates housing demand

Valdosta serves a 15 to 17 county region for retail, health care and tourism, and a few large institutions anchor local housing demand. Valdosta State University has over 11,000 students, Moody Air Force Base has over 6,500 military and civilian employees, and South Georgia Medical Center has over 2,600 employees. More than 12,000 military retirees and family members live in Lowndes County and the counties next to it.

Think of student renters, military households and hospital staff as three separate pools of buyers or tenants. A house near campus, near the base gates or near the medical center can be marketed to the group that fits its location, and a cash buyer who plans to rent it can take it in its current condition.

Valdosta also has six historic districts: Valdosta Commercial, Fairview, North Patterson, Brookwood North, Southside and East End. If your house sits in or near one, ask the city about any review that applies before you plan exterior changes.

Valdosta housing numbers

Owners occupy 41.7 percent of Valdosta's homes, so renters hold the larger share. Each number below is a 2020 to 2024 estimate unless the label gives a date.

Property maintenance rules

Valdosta enforces a property maintenance ordinance that caps grass and weeds at eight inches and requires you to cut to the street or sidewalk, including adjacent ditches. A complaint triggers a site visit and then a certified letter that gives the owner 10 business days to comply.

With nearly 600 miles of right-of-way in the city, Valdosta leans on owners to care for the strip beside their lots. The owner is responsible for the right-of-way next to the lot, and the city asks that clippings not be blown into the street or storm drain. Community Safety takes these calls at 229-259-3554.

Permits before you sell

Permits matter at resale. Buyers and lenders often ask for proof that alterations met code, and with no permit and inspection on record an owner may have to redo work or lose the sale. A permit is needed for roofs, accessory buildings, in-ground pools, foundations, patios, and gas, mechanical, plumbing or electrical systems.

  • Permit Office hours run 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, phone 229-259-3506.
  • A homeowner may pull a permit only to do the work personally, and only in the home they will occupy. Buying a permit for someone else's work is illegal in Georgia.
  • New construction or additions need a zoning approval letter.

If you already did work without a permit, call the Permit Office before listing so you know what a buyer's inspector or lender may ask for.

Lowndes County property taxes

Assessment notices arrive from Lowndes County in May, and you get 45 days to contest the value. Tax bills are mailed early in October, and real estate bills are usually due November 15.

Missing the date costs 1 percent a month in interest. Ninety days late adds a 10 percent penalty, except on homesteaded property with a bill under $500, and the county may file a lien and start a tax sale through its Delinquent Tax Office.

Assessed value equals 40 percent of the January 1 market value, and one mill means $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. A contested value goes to the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and later to superior court. Before you pick a closing date, call the Lowndes County Tax Commissioner for the current homestead deadline and your parcel's balance.

Steps for a clean closing

  1. Order your deed copy from the Clerk of Superior Court and confirm the name and parcel match your records.
  2. Call the Lowndes County Tax Commissioner for your parcel's balance and the current homestead deadline.
  3. Ask the Permit Office whether roofs, pools, patios or system replacements on your lot have a permit and a passed inspection.
  4. Walk the lot against the eight inch grass rule and clear the right-of-way strip beside it.
  5. Collect bids, compare what each leaves you after payoff and costs, and pick a closing date you can actually meet.

Doing the first four before you talk to buyers, ideally a few weeks ahead, means the offer you accept is less likely to be renegotiated at the last minute. Cash buyers can often close on the date you choose, while a financed buyer's lender sets the schedule.

Deed and transfer tax

The Clerk of Superior Court at the Lowndes County Courthouse records your deed once Georgia's transfer tax is paid. The Department of Revenue page prints the rate.

The seller carries that liability unless the sales contract moves it. A PT-61 form goes in electronically through the clerks' cooperative authority. Ask your title agent for the payoff letter, the tax proration and the transfer tax figure ahead of closing so none of them arrives as a surprise at the table on closing day.

If a tenant lives in the house, tell your buyer whether the tenant stays or leaves at closing, and pass along the lease so the buyer can read the term and notice rules.

Frequently asked questions

Is a permit needed to replace a Valdosta roof before a sale?

Yes. Roofs are on the city's list of work needing a building permit. A permit with a passed inspection on file gives a buyer or lender proof that the work met code.

How tall can grass be on a Valdosta lot?

Grass and weeds may not exceed eight inches under Ordinance No. 2011-37. The city follows a complaint with a site visit and a certified letter giving 10 business days to bring the lot into compliance.

When do Lowndes County property tax bills come due?

Bills are mailed in early October, and real estate is usually due November 15. Interest of 1 percent a month follows.

Can a tenant-occupied Valdosta house be sold?

Yes. With owners occupying 41.7 percent of Valdosta homes, sales with tenants in place are common. Read the lease terms and tell your buyer whether the tenant stays or leaves at closing.

Who pays Georgia's transfer tax when a Valdosta house sells?

The seller, under state law, though a contract may assign it to the buyer. It must be paid before the deed is recorded, and the Department of Revenue page shows the rate.

The mid-2025 estimate is 51,792 residents, only 0.3% above the 51,643 counted for April 2020, so the population is close to flat. Without much vacant land to build on, sales here are mostly resales, and a house with deferred repairs competes against updated ones at the same price.

Nightly rentals are banned

Dunwoody's Code of Ordinances forbids short-term rentals of single-family and multi-family homes. That covers stays under 30 days booked through Vrbo, Airbnb and HomeToGo, and the city enforces the ban when someone complains.

The code also bars party houses, meaning residences used for a commercial party that guests pay to attend. Those events belong at special event facilities with special event permits, and private social gatherings are outside the rule. The city tells residents to call 911 about noise or traffic.

For a seller, that removes nightly-rental investors from the buyer pool. Anyone seeking income is left with long-term leases, so a house with a tenant on a standard lease is pitched that way. The city sends visitors to the DeKalb County School District, which calls itself the third largest district in Georgia, with more than 90,300 students and 137 schools and centers. Buyers also ask about public spaces. The city's site features Dunwoody Village, Brook Run Park, and a sculpture exhibit at the Dunwoody Nature Center at Dunwoody Park. The Dunwoody Preservation Trust, a local nonprofit, runs the historic Donaldson-Bannister Farm as an event venue.

How DeKalb property tax is billed and paid

Because Dunwoody lies in DeKalb County, the county's Tax Commissioner issues and collects the bill. It goes to the person recorded as owner each January 1 and to the present owner if that is someone else. A bill that never shows up still has to be paid.

Current-year payments run August 15 through November 15 in two installments, and the first must be paid before the second. Late amounts draw penalties or interest, and paying only part of a bill is allowed. Receipt by the due date is what counts, and for mailed checks the county reads the USPS postmark.

Paying online by e-check costs nothing extra, while cards carry a percentage fee. Earlier-year balances go to a separate delinquent collections division.

Paperwork to pull together first

The city runs an online portal for licenses and permits and posts a searchable code of ordinances. If the house has an unpermitted addition or an open complaint, learn that before the buyer's inspector does.

From offer to closing day

Once you accept an offer, the steps are simple. A title company searches the deed history, your closing attorney prepares the settlement statement, and payoffs for the mortgage and any liens are ordered. Property tax is prorated or assigned in the contract, and Georgia's transfer tax is paid before the deed is recorded.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which are usually the slowest steps. That is why closing dates can be short. A financed buyer adds an inspection, an appraisal and a loan approval, and any of them can reopen the price.

If you rent the house out, give the buyer the lease and deposit details early. If you live there, agree on a handover date and a final walkthrough so nothing is left to argue about on the last day.

Ask the closing attorney for the settlement statement a few days ahead and read every line.

What you give up with a cash bid

Cash brings speed and fewer moving parts, and a listing brings the chance of a higher price. With home values this high, the gap between the two can be wide, so get actual numbers instead of assuming.

Ask every buyer for written terms: closing costs, days to close, any inspection or financing contingency, and the consequence of walking away. Then work out your take-home after the mortgage payoff, tax bills and liens, using figures from your lender and the closing attorney.

Owners who are relocating, settling an estate or racing a deadline tend to prize certainty. Owners with a move-in-ready house and flexible timing usually do better on the open market.

Working from home? Check the business license

The city requires a business license for any business with a physical location inside it. A home-based business should confirm its status with the licensing office before a sale, because a buyer will ask whether any certificate transfers or ends.

The Planning Commission and the city's list of zoning and variance decisions show what is under review. Read them if a rezoning or redevelopment is happening near your street, since buyers sometimes ask.

No. The city code forbids short-term rentals of houses and multi-family homes, including stays under 30 days booked through Vrbo, Airbnb and similar services, and the city acts on complaints.

Which office collects property tax on a Dunwoody house?

The DeKalb County Tax Commissioner. Current-year payments run August 15 through November 15, with two installments allowed and penalties on late amounts.

The DeKalb County School District. Your street address decides which schools your home feeds.

Yes. Hand the buyer the lease and deposit details. A buyer keeping the tenant needs the terms, and one wanting a vacant house will price that in.

The fastest sound way to sell in Gainesville

Choose among a retail listing, a sale you manage yourself and a cash purchase by weighing your deadline against the work the house needs. Gainesville is the Hall County seat, so deeds, tax bills and appeals pass through Hall County offices along with the city's.

Gainesville sits beside Lake Lanier and is a renter-majority city, so a seller should expect both owner-occupant and landlord buyers. A house that needs little work can do well on the open market. A house with roof, foundation or system problems may sit longer and lose ground to nearby listings.

  • Retail listing: biggest audience, with inspection and lender clocks you do not control.

Lake Lanier and what buyers like about Gainesville

Gainesville began as the village of Mule Camp Springs and was chartered under its present name on November 30, 1821, as the seat of newly created Hall County. A railroad arrived in 1871, and poultry became the dominant industry after World War II. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers finished Lake Lanier in 1957, and the lake covers more than 38,000 acres.

  • Lake access and the greenway system that links downtown parks to the lake are marketing points the city itself promotes.
  • Brenau University, the University of North Georgia and Lanier Technical College give the area a steady education base.

Which school system serves a Gainesville address?

Gainesville has two public systems nearby, Gainesville City Schools and Hall County Schools, and the attendance zone for the exact address decides which one a child uses. Families must enroll a child in the school where the child is zoned unless a choice-enrollment request is approved.

The city system registers students through one central online process and publishes an attendance zone map. Its elementary schools include Centennial Arts Academy, Enota Multiple Intelligences Academy, Fair Street International Academy, Gainesville Exploration Academy, Mundy Mill Arts Academy and New Holland Knowledge Academy, followed by Gainesville Middle School and Gainesville High School. Hall County Schools runs its own attendance zones outside the city system.

Do not guess a school assignment in a listing. Tell buyers to check the Gainesville City School System zone map and Hall County Schools before they rely on any address.

Hall County property tax and appeals

Hall County appraises a Gainesville house at full fair market value on January 1 and taxes 40 percent of that figure. Owners inside the city limits also receive a separate City of Gainesville statement.

  • Value measured as of: January 1.
  • Appraisal level: 100% of fair market value, with 40% of it taxed.
  • Time to contest the value: 45 days after the notice date.
  • 2026 statements mailed: October 15, 2026, with payment due December 15, 2026.
  • Typical year: mailed September 15, due November 15.

Values follow recent property sales. The assessors only set value, while the county, the city and the school boards set the tax rates. One mill equals $1 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value.

File an appeal on qPublic, by mail to the assessors' post office box, or at 2875 Browns Bridge Road. Grounds accepted are value, uniformity, taxability, denial of an exemption and covenant. The target is the valuation rather than the tax amount. A homestead exemption can be filed in person or on qPublic, and it must be on file before the 45-day window ends to count for the current year.

Who pays the Hall County bill when you sell

Liability for a year's bill rests with whoever owned the property of record on January 1, and the closing papers or closing attorney settle who actually pays. A 2026 seller who wants the buyer billed has to send the sale documents to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days after the due date, which works out to March 15, 2027.

When the papers clearly move liability, the seller drops off the bill. Anything arriving after that date cannot be considered. A property under appeal is billed at the lower of 85 percent of the 2026 value or 100 percent of the 2025 value, and unpaid appeal bills still gather monthly interest once the due date passes.

A state transfer tax adds one more seller-side cost at recording, though the sales contract may place it on the buyer.

When to call a cash buyer

Call one when the house is hard to finance, hard to show or caught in a family situation. Tenant-occupied sales come up often in a renter-majority city.

  • A rental where showings would disturb the tenant.
  • A Hall County house inherited by a faraway heir.
  • A house a mortgage lender will not finance after inspection.
  • A move date driven by a job or family change.

Read the bid closely, see which closing charges fall to you, and set its net beside a listing's net after commission and repairs. Keep the right to decline, and ask for every term in writing before you commit.

Selling a Gainesville rental

Many Gainesville sales involve a tenant. Start with the lease: note when it ends, how much deposit you hold, and whether the tenant is current. Any buyer will ask for those three facts, and a cash buyer may take the house with the lease still running.

If you want the house empty at closing, say so in the contract and agree on a move-out date in writing. If the tenant stays, show the lease to each buyer before they make an offer. Showings are the other pressure point: a financed buyer needs access for photos, an inspection and an appraisal, while a cash buyer usually needs far fewer visits.

Yes. Owners inside Gainesville city limits get a city statement in addition to the Hall County one.

Who owes the 2026 tax if I sell a Gainesville house during 2026?

The January 1, 2026 owner of record is liable, and the closing papers decide who pays. The seller should send sale documents to the Tax Commissioner by March 15, 2027.

What is the deadline to dispute a Hall County valuation?

Forty-five days after the date printed on the assessment notice. Appeals go in through qPublic, by mail or in person, and they dispute the value, not the tax bill.

Which school does a Gainesville address feed?

It depends on the zone. Use the Gainesville City School System zone map, and check Hall County Schools for addresses outside the city system.

Can a Gainesville house with tenants be sold?

Yes. Only 39.2 percent of Gainesville homes are owner occupied, so rentals sell often. Review the lease and deposit and tell each buyer the unit is occupied.

A bungalow near the square and a subdivision house out by the bypass will not match those averages, so look at what sold nearest to you.

Older houses and historic districts

Newnan's nickname is the "City of Homes," and antebellum and early 20th century houses survive in several historic districts. Cotton money and the railroad made it one of the richest towns per person in America by the mid 1800s, and the R.D. Cole company, which began as a sawmill in 1854, built most of the city's homes from the 1880s into the early 1900s. That explains the shared woodwork details buyers notice.

The city lists seven districts, and several are residential:

  • Cole Town grew around the Cole company and carries its woodwork.
  • College-Temple, laid out in 1828, has tree-lined streets, churches and a former academy lot.
  • Greenville-LaGrange covers 61 acres, with the oldest and grandest houses on the main streets.
  • Platinum Point is a 43-acre district of early 20th century houses north of town.
  • Newnan Cotton Mill and Mill Village includes a mill now converted to loft apartments.
  • Chalk Level, about 261 acres in southeast Newnan, joined the Georgia Register of Historic Places on October 24, 2025 and the National Register on January 29, 2026.

If your house is in one of them and exterior changes are planned, ask Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 whether design review applies.

Building permits and tree rules

  • A ResChek or Comchek compliance report
  • Contractor licenses and a subcontractor list

Records of past work help at sale time, because unrecorded additions tend to show up under a buyer's inspection.

Tree work has its own rule. A homeowner pays no fee to remove trees on a single-family lot until more than five come down at once in a calendar year, while anyone paid to cut trees needs a permit for each one eight inches across or larger. Specimen trees follow separate rules.

Coweta homestead and senior school tax exemptions

A homestead exemption stays with the person, so the buyer files a new application with the Assessors' Office. Each individual or married couple gets just one.

Assessments and tax bills

The Assessors' Office at 37 Perry Street sets values, and the Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive bills and collects. Assessment notices go out in early summer and open a 45-day appeal window, and each notice states its own deadline.

October brings the bills. One goes to the legal owner as of January 1 and another to the current owner on the Assessors' file, so a house sold after New Year's produces two. A parcel with an unresolved appeal gets a temporary bill set at 85 percent of the proposed value, and the final ruling produces a refund or an additional charge. Residential homestead bills for 2026 also carry the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant credit.

Homeowners with escrow should forward the bill to their servicer, because lenders often pay just weeks ahead of the deadline. Card payments add 2.5 percent (3 percent for American Express), and an online e-check costs $1.50. Call the Assessors at 770-254-2680 or the Tax Commissioner at 770-254-2670.

Clearing out a house before listing

Cleanout is simple in Newnan. Junk pickup needs no appointment: set items by the street on your regular collection day. Yard debris and bulk waste go through the Sanitation Department at 770-253-0327. Bagged trash must sit inside the cart, and the city will not take anything left beside it, although a second cart can be added. The AMWASTE service puts trash and recycling in one container.

Burning is allowed only with a permit from the Fire Marshal, reachable at 770-253-1851, extension 302. If a basement or outbuilding is full, start early so inspectors and buyers can see the structure.

From offer to closing in Newnan

  2. Check whether the house sits in a historic district before you promise exterior work.
  3. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether the house will produce two bills this year.
  4. Have the closing attorney set out in the contract who pays each bill and the transfer tax.
  5. Clear the house, since a buyer's inspector needs to see every room and outbuilding.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and most repair requests, so it moves faster when the house is dated or needs work. A listing reaches more buyers, but the lender sets the closing date.

Recording the deed in Coweta County

The Superior Court Clerk's Real Estate Division keeps every Coweta record and files documents daily in arrival order. Posted fees include $25 for a deed, $10 for a plat and $1 a page for copies, and personal checks are refused. The PT-61 transfer tax form must be e-filed with every title change. Self-filers need identity verification, while attorneys, lenders, title companies and brokers may file on paper.

Georgia's transfer tax, $1 per first $1,000 with 10 cents per further $100, shows on the settlement statement too. Owners can also sign up for free real estate fraud alerts through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. The closing attorney or title company typically files the deed after a Newnan closing.

Possibly, because Coweta bills the January 1 owner of record and also mails a bill to the newest owner. Put the payment duty in the contract and settle it at closing.

Each notice opens a 45-day window from its own date, and the deadline is printed on the notice. Call 770-254-2680 for help reading it.

They may. The city lists seven districts, including Cole Town, College-Temple, Downtown and Chalk Level. Call Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 before exterior work.

Speed humps work differently. The Georgia Department of Revenue treats the real estate transfer tax as the seller's cost unless the contract says otherwise, and it must be paid before the deed is recorded. Ask the Gwinnett clerk of superior court for current recording fees, and have your attorney e-file the PT-61.

Property tax and who pays when the house sells

The county mails tax notices in early autumn to whoever is the owner of record on January 1, and payment falls due 60 days after mailing. Each notice prints its own due date.

When a property changes hands mid-year, buyer and seller decide between themselves who owes what, normally at the closing. The Tax Commissioner stays out of that split. The bill adds up levies from each governing body at your address, which for a Douglasville house means the county commissioners, the school board, and the city's mayor and council.

The spring assessment notice carries only an estimate. The real amount waits on each body's millage rate, so the estimate and the final bill can differ.
