Homestead exemptions and your sale

A homestead exemption trims the taxable value of the home where you live. The county offers these kinds:

  • Standard homestead exemption.
  • Senior exemptions at age 62 and at age 65, with a fixed-income version for age 65 that carries income requirements.
  • Disability exemption, with required medical certification.
  • Disabled veteran exemption, with a letter from the VA showing service-connected disability benefits.
  • Surviving spouse exemption for spouses of service members killed in action and of police officers or firefighters killed in the line of duty.

To get the benefit for a given tax year you must be both owner and resident on January 1 and file by April 1, although the office takes applications all year. Exemptions roll over without a new filing unless ownership changes or eligibility ends. The next owner files fresh after closing, so name the tax year your exemption covers in the contract.

If your Douglasville taxes are past due

The Tax Commissioner's website has a Delinquent Taxes and Sales section covering properties with unpaid taxes, upcoming tax sales and an excess funds list. Look up your parcel before choosing how to sell, because an unpaid balance changes what a buyer or title company demands.

Selling can clear back taxes, since the balance comes out of the buyer's payment. Starting early keeps more options open, because penalties and a pending tax sale shrink your window. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the exact payoff before you name a price.

A lender's foreclosure timeline is separate and may be the shorter clock. If a notice has arrived from your lender, set it beside your loan statement, since a fast sale has to satisfy both.

Weighing a cash bid against a listing

Compare what lands in your account and when. A listing can produce a bigger price but adds repair bills, showings and financing delays. A cash bid is usually lower and removes the repairs and the waiting.

Get every offer in writing and ask each buyer the same things: who covers closing costs, what condition the house must be in at handover, whether an inspection can cancel the deal, and what happens if the title has a flaw. With tenants, ask how the buyer will treat the lease. With an inherited house, confirm that the person signing has legal authority.

Buyers here include families and investors, so a leased rental suits one group and a vacant house suits the other.

What is the payment window for Douglas County property tax?

The deadline is 60 days after notices go out in early autumn. Each notice prints the exact date, so read yours rather than relying on a general date.

Who owes the tax if a Douglasville house sells mid-year?

Buyer and seller agree on the split, typically at the closing. The Tax Commissioner does not referee it.

What is the deadline for a homestead exemption in Douglas County?

April 1. You need to be owner and resident on January 1 of that year, and missing April 1 forfeits the exemption for the year.

How much is the typical Douglasville home worth?

The five-year figure ending 2024 is $359,200. Age, condition and location move individual houses well away from it.

Can a Douglasville house with open code or permit problems be sold?

Yes. Ask the city's Building Division or Code Compliance what is open, then tell the buyer. Cash buyers often take the house with those items unresolved.

About 41,445 people live in Mulberry by the 2025 estimate, five percent above the 39,468 in the April 2020 base. Those totals say little about what your street sells for, so ask a local agent for sold homes within a few blocks.

Is my house inside the City of Mulberry?

The city offers an "Am I in Mulberry?" web app, and staff will confirm an address or parcel number at 770-341-9640. Since January 1, 2025, the city has handled the following inside its limits:

  • Zoning, rezonings, special use permits and variances

Gwinnett keeps plan review and inspections for fire, water and sewer. Court challenges to the city charter are pending, so confirm any permit question with the city before you rely on an answer. Put the permit paperwork for the house in one folder before you list.

Zoning and permit rules

Mulberry adopted its own zoning map on July 16, 2026, so a zoning label from the county days may have changed. The city's One Map web app shows the zoning layer for any parcel, and staff can read it back by address.

The city's FAQ covers the points inspectors and buyers raise most often:

  • Permit applications are uploaded through the SagesGov portal, and a permit lapses after six months of inactivity.
  • An inspection must happen within six months of issuance, and requests are due by 4:00 PM two business days ahead.
  • Work started without a required permit risks stop work orders and fines, and illegal work may have to be removed.
  • Deck repairs need a permit when structural parts are involved or most boards are replaced.
  • The city allows one accessory dwelling unit per primary home, and the primary home must be owner occupied.
  • Hard surface in the front yard of a single-family house generally cannot exceed 35 percent.
  • Projects that disturb an acre or more, or ground within 200 feet of state waters, need an erosion and sediment control plan reviewed by the state.

A buyer who wants a rezoning faces a slower road. Staff require a pre-application meeting, review takes about two months, and the department takes just four such applications a month.

Bills go out in late summer for a fall due date. Late balances gain 0.81 percent interest monthly, and a 5 percent penalty applies after 120 days and again every further 120 days, up to 20 percent. Who pays the tax bill when a Mulberry house sells?

The January 1 owner is on the hook for the whole year, and Gwinnett bills both the old and new owner after a sale. If the bill goes unpaid, the lien lands on the January 1 owner unless, within 90 days of the due date, the commissioner receives:

  • Acceptable proof that the buyer assumed the liability
  • A deed in the new owner's name
  • Confirmation that the deed was properly recorded

Contract wording makes the difference. The commissioner accepts "Payment of all outstanding taxes and assessments not paid at settlement and those incurred in the future are assumed by purchaser." It rejects lines that say the parties "agree to adjust the pro-rations amongst themselves." Ask your closing attorney for the accepted style and keep a copy of the settlement statement.

The state levies $1 on the first $1,000 of price and 10 cents on every added $100 or fraction of it. What to fix before listing

Walk the property as a code officer would. The city flags grass and weeds over 12 inches, vehicles parked without a current tag, and yard trimmings left on a street or sidewalk, and it expects unpaved front-yard areas to stay covered with grass or ground cover.

Then gather records for any addition, deck, pool or fence. Pools need a permit and an approved location plan, fences need an approved application, and removing trees may need a limited land disturbance permit, so call the city first. Gaps in that file tend to surface at a buyer's inspection, and sorting them out early keeps a contract on track.

Choosing a sale route

A listing reaches the widest set of buyers but adds showings, repair requests and a commission. A private sale keeps the commission and hands pricing and contracts to you. A cash investor buys as-is on a short timeline, with a price set by repair and resale costs. Collect at least two written offers, compare who pays closing costs, and let a Georgia closing attorney prepare the deed. Do I get permits from Gwinnett County or from Mulberry?

Inside the city limits, permits go through Mulberry's SagesGov portal. Gwinnett still performs fire, water and sewer plan review and inspections. Use the city's address lookup if you are unsure about your parcel.

Will I get a tax bill after I sell?

If you owned the house on January 1, yes. Gwinnett mails a bill to both owners, and you stay responsible unless assumption proof, the new deed and the recording are all in place within 90 days of the due date.

What deadline applies to a Gwinnett assessment appeal?

Forty-five days from the date at the top of the annual notice. Appeals can be made online, in person or by mail. Reach the assessors at 770-822-7200.

Selling routes for a Milton property

A Milton owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase of the property as it stands. With large lots and high values, the choice often rests on how much prep the property needs before it shows well.

An agent listing is the usual path for updated homes, with staging, showings and a lender-driven close. A private sale works when you already have a buyer or want to control showings. A cash buyer takes an as-is house with deferred maintenance, estate complications or tenants, with fewer repair negotiations. About 41,266 people live in Milton by the 2025 estimate, essentially flat against the April 2020 base of 41,292. Most of the city's growth came before 2020. Owners occupy 72.5% of homes, and the typical owned home is valued at $789,000. Owners pay about $3,176 a month with a mortgage and $1,128 without, gross rent is $2,065, and median household income is $171,295 across 15,225 households of about 2.72 people each.

At this price level, a few percentage points between two offers is a large sum, and unfinished repairs tend to show up in the price a buyer proposes. Buyers here also expect a well-kept property, so a house that needs work may suit a buyer who takes it as-is.

Rural zoning and septic systems

About 85% of Milton's more than 39 square miles is agriculturally zoned, which means residential lots must be at least one acre. The vast majority of the land is on septic, which requires parcels of an acre or more. If your Milton house is on septic, locate the tank records and any recent pumping or inspection paperwork, since a buyer's inspector may ask for them.

Milton sits between Cherokee County to the north and west, Forsyth County to the east, Roswell to the southwest and Alpharetta to the south. State Route 400, a short drive away, is the road buyers mention most.

Tree removal rules

The City Council approved the Tree Canopy Conservation Ordinance on August 3, 2020, and it took effect immediately. The Tree Conservation page answers common questions: whether you need a permit to remove trees on residential property, whether trees beside a stream or lake can be removed, whether a fee applies, and whether replanting is required. Ask the City Arborist, at the contact on that page, before removing trees while you prepare the house for sale. Cutting a tree to improve curb appeal can cause trouble if a permit was needed, and a buyer's attorney may ask for the permit paperwork or the arborist's answer in writing.

Fulton's Clerk of Superior Court records a Milton deed once Georgia's transfer tax is paid. The tax is $1 on the first $1,000 (or fraction of it) and 10 cents on every further $100 (or fraction of it).

Once you accept an offer, the buyer's side orders an inspection and a title search. If an appeal of your value is open, the bill may be temporary, so ask the Board of Assessors how it will be resolved before you promise a figure to the buyer.

After closing, the Fulton Clerk of Superior Court records the deed once the transfer tax is paid. A cash sale follows the same legal steps but skips the lender's appraisal, which can shorten the schedule when the house has deferred maintenance a lender would question.

Preparing a Milton house for market

Pull together the deed, the latest Fulton bill, any septic tank records and permit history. Walk the lot and decide which tree work, if any, needs the City Arborist first. Then ask the Tax Commissioner for the live bill and balance so the closing attorney can settle it from proceeds. A buyer in this market may also ask how the lot drains and where the boundaries sit, so have any survey on hand. One acre in agriculturally zoned areas, which cover about 85% of the city. Confirm your parcel's zoning with Community Development at 678-242-2545.

Forty-five days from the date on the notice. The right ends once that period runs out, so mark the date the day the notice arrives. Filing works online, in person or by mail.

Selling a house in Peachtree City

A Peachtree City house sells with extras few other Georgia markets have: a village identity, a link to the city's path network and often a registered golf cart. Owners generally compare a standard listing, a private sale and a cash offer. The 2025 estimate puts the population at 40,880, up 6.9% from 38,241 in the 2020 base.

This is a city of owners. Homeowners occupy 72.1% of housing units, the median owner-occupied value is $482,500 and median household income reaches $113,987. Renting costs a median $2,086 a month, so some buyers price the two options against each other. In a listing, name the village and the nearest path link, because both shape how buyers picture daily life. The villages are Aberdeen, Braelinn, Glenloch, Kedron and Wilksmoor.

Golf cart paths and cart registration

The city counts more than 100 miles of shared-use paths and about 11,000 registered carts. A seller with a cart has paperwork to finish, and a buyer shopping for one should know the rules:

  • New cart registrations are completed in person at City Hall, and owners must be 18 or older.
  • A cart must be registered within 10 days of purchase.
  • A seller must report the sale or removal of decals within 10 days using the Cart Release Form.
  • A move requires a change of address notice within 60 days.
  • Decals go on both the front and rear of the cart.
  • Low-speed vehicles may use the paths if limited to 20 mph, insured, tagged through the Fayette County Tag Office, driven by someone with a valid license and fitted with an amber strobe light.

Residents pay $45 for a three-year renewal covering 2026 through 2028. A buyer who lives outside the city and pays no Peachtree City property tax owes a yearly path user fee on top of registration.

ChargeAmount

Short-term rental permits

A buyer who wants to run a short-term rental from a Peachtree City house needs a city permit. Stays of 30 consecutive days or less count as short-term, and since January 1, 2025 every such rental needs a permit, with a citywide cap of 135. Operators who could prove rentals and tax payments before the ordinance passed on November 7, 2024 went first. If the count already exceeds 135, all keep their permits and no new ones issue until it drops below the cap.

Rentals are allowed in residential zoning districts, but detached structures, guest houses, recreational vehicles and trailers cannot be rented this way. A permit lasts 730 days. Applicants provide:

  • The completed application and a guest occupancy agreement under O.C.G.A. 43-21-3.2
  • A copy of the deed showing the applicant owns the property
  • A notarized criminal background check consent and a notarized tax payment and ordinance affidavit
  • Homeowner association approval, if one applies

The Building Department and Fire Marshal also inspect the property. Fines rise with repeat violations, up to $500 for a first, $750 for a second and $1,000 for a third in 12 months, and the third also brings a 24-month revocation. If you market the house as an income property, ask city staff whether the permit follows the owner or the address before you tell a buyer it transfers.

Assessments and appeals in Fayette County

Fayette's Assessors' Office values real and personal property and takes homestead applications, while the Tax Commissioner bills and collects at 770-461-3652. Residential and commercial notices are mailed once a year, and every notice opens a 45-day appeal window. The written appeal must be signed, dated and received inside that window. Call the Fayette Assessors at 770-305-5376 with questions.

Homestead exemption and tiers

Fayette no longer cuts homestead applications off on April 1. If you owned and occupied the home on January 1, you can apply up to the end of that year's appeal window. Someone who moved in later applies after the next January 1. A recently purchased home needs a recorded warranty deed or settlement statement along with a Georgia driver's license showing the address.

Fayette's exemption page lists several tiers that a seller can point buyers toward:

  • The basic L1 homestead exemption reduces state and school M&O assessed value by $2,000 and county and fire M&O by $5,000.
  • The L7 floating exemption limits yearly growth of the school portion of a homesteaded value to the lesser of 3% or inflation, plus improvements.
  • Owners 62 by January 1 may qualify for a school tax reduction that rises from $2,000 to $4,000, and owners 65 may qualify for a 50% school tax reduction.
  • A 100% disabled veteran may qualify for an exemption of $126,526.

The Assessors can tell you the codes that appear on your bill.

Georgia transfer tax in Peachtree City

Before a deed is recorded, the clerk of superior court collects Georgia's transfer tax and stamps proof of payment on the document. The seller is liable, though many contracts push it to the buyer. Questions about the electronic PT-61 go to the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority at (800) 304-5174.

Ask the Fayette County clerk for the current recording fee list, and review the tax lines on the settlement statement before you sign.

Papers to prepare before you list

Gather the deed, your latest Fayette tax bill, and the exemption codes on it. If a cart stays with the house, find the registration and decal paperwork and the release forms. If the house has been rented short term, locate the permit file, the guest occupancy agreement and any homeowner association approval. A buyer's attorney will ask for these, and a cash buyer will use them to judge risk. Having them ready keeps a deal from stalling late in the process.

Listing, private sale or cash?

A house in good shape near the paths and lakes has the best odds on the open market, at the cost of prep work, showings and repair talks. A private sale saves the commission. A cash buyer suits a deadline, an inherited house or a property too worn for lender financing, with a price that reflects the buyer's repair and resale costs. Get terms in writing, and settle with your attorney how the cart registration and any rental permit will pass to the new owner.

Frequently asked questions

Does my golf cart registration change when I sell the house?

If the cart goes with the house, yes. The seller reports the sale or removes the decals within 10 days, and the buyer registers within 10 days. The Ownership Release and Cart Release forms apply, and new registrations are completed at City Hall.

How many short-term rental permits does Peachtree City allow?

The ordinance caps them at 135. Operators with documented rentals before November 7, 2024 had priority, and permits renew every 730 days. Ask the city whether a permit can follow a property to a new owner.

How long do I have to appeal a Fayette value?

Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a Peachtree City sale?

The seller is liable by statute, and many contracts assign it to the buyer. It is paid before the deed is recorded.

Canton has grown fast, from 22,958 people in 2010 to 32,973 in 2020, with an estimate of 40,778 for mid-2025. A house here competes with steady newer construction, so ask for comparable sales that match your house's age and size.

Projects that shape Canton demand

Canton is a Cherokee County city, and part of its historic downtown lies inside a National Historic District. The city's FY2026 capital plan includes an Etowah River pedestrian bridge, design work on State Route 140 in North Canton, the first projects from the Transportation Master Plan, waterline upgrades at Highway 20 and I-575, sidewalk and road improvements along Hickory Flat Highway and Marietta Road, a new South Canton Park, and a rewrite of the Unified Development Code.

A house near one of those corridors invites buyer questions about construction timing, so get the schedule from the city before listing. The city runs its own water, wastewater, stormwater and sanitation utilities, and the same plan funds a water pollution control plant expansion and an elevated water tank at Ridge Pine. Questions about utility service, and impact fees on new construction, belong with the city.

Canton housing costs

Canton values and rents run above the national midpoints, while incomes sit close to them. Every figure covers 2020 to 2024, so it trails current sales.

  • Homeownership rate: 55.6 percent in Canton, 65.2 percent nationally.

Who bills Canton property tax

Under a 2017 intergovernmental agreement, Cherokee County bills and collects Canton's city property tax, and the county assessor sets values. The millage rate is applied to 40 percent of the property's fair market value.

Canton's city rate was 8.5 mills in 1997 and 5.4 mills for 2017 through 2024, and the city proposed 5.25 for 2025. The county's 2.888-mill fire rate is not reduced by the senior exemption. Ask the tax commissioner which rates apply for the year you sell.

The exemptions and freeze above belong to the owner who applied. Call the Cherokee County Tax Assessors office at 678-493-6120 to learn how a change of owner is handled for your parcel, and get the amount due from the tax commissioner so the settlement statement can split it at closing.

Buyers and closing attorneys ask for the same handful of papers, and having them on hand keeps a short sale short. Gather your latest Cherokee County assessment notice, proof of any exemption you hold, a copy of any lease with the rent record, and permits for work done on the house. If you ever put in a deck, a finished basement or new wiring, find the permit now, since an unpermitted job can slow a lender and will come up with a cash buyer too.

Then take the steps in order. Choose your route, get a price from comparable sales or written cash offers, pick a closing attorney, and ask the tax commissioner for the current amount due. A cash buyer pays without a loan, so there is no appraisal to wait on and no lender to approve the file. That is why a cash sale can close on a date you pick, usually in exchange for a price under what a retail buyer might pay.

Selling a Canton house with repairs or tenants

Houses with deferred repairs, tenants in place or an estate behind them are where an as-is sale earns its place. A regular listing can still close in these cases, but loan-backed buyers tend to ask for repairs after the inspection, and a tenant's lease limits showings. If a lease is running, give every buyer the lease and the rent record at the start. If the owner has died, the person handling the estate may need to settle authority to sell before any contract is signed, so raise that with the closing attorney early.

Compare what you would net on each path, not the asking price. Repairs, commission, carrying costs while the house sits and the property tax bill all come out of the final number. A lower cash offer that closes next month can leave you with as much as a higher listing price that takes longer and loses some of its value to repair requests.

Permits, zoning and recording

Canton's Community Development department runs an online permitting and licensing portal, so any work done to ready a house for sale should go through it. If a buyer plans to rezone, subdivide or annex a parcel, ask Community Development how current rules apply, because the city has reviewed growth patterns, land use maps and zoning categories in recent years. Public hearing applications were taken on the first business day of each month, and the process ran three months.

At recording, the Cherokee County clerk will not accept a deed until Georgia's transfer tax is paid, after which the clerk stamps a certification onto it. State guidance makes the seller liable unless the contract assigns the tax to the buyer.

Forty-five days, starting on the date of the Cherokee County assessment notice, which usually arrives around mid-June. A homestead application can go in during the same window.

Yes, in two forms. The county offers a school tax exemption to owners 62 and older with five years of homestead, and the city has a senior exemption on fair market value up to $280,000, filed by April 1.

How big is Canton's population?

About 40,800. The mid-2025 estimate is 40,778, a 23.7 percent gain on the April 2020 base of 32,957.

Yes, if the buyer pays cash and accepts the property as-is. A listing can close with repairs undone as well, though inspections often bring repair requests, so compare what you net each way.

The city uses a separate Short-term Rental Application for that use. Anyone intending to continue the rental should ask the Business License Division at (770) 592-6054 what the buyer must file.

Cherokee County looks to the January 1 owner for the bill, and the sale contract decides how the cost is shared. Ask the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner for the exact bill and balance before you sign.

Rome and Floyd County share a Unified Land Development Code, and the city posts it with a 2040 Comprehensive Plan on its Board of Adjustments page. Planning staff take appointments for questions about a property, a project or a request.

Requests that go to the Board of Adjustments include appeals of an administrator's decision, special exceptions, hardship variances and flood protection variances. It meets on the third Thursday at 2:30 in the upstairs Commission Chambers at City Hall, 601 Broad Street. An application must arrive by 5:00 p.m. on the 25th, and the earliest hearing is two months after that date.

  • Special exceptions: relief from setbacks, building height, lot width, street frontage, buffers, signs and parking requirements.

If your house has a nonconforming addition, a garage apartment or a setback problem, raise it with planning staff before a buyer's survey does. A cash buyer can live with the problem, and a lender may not.

Send a letter to the Floyd County Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. Allowed grounds are taxability, uniformity, value, or a denied homestead exemption.

Forty-five days, counted from the date the notice was mailed, by letter to the Board of Assessors. A changed value opens a further 21 days to contest the new figure.

The joint Rome and Floyd County Board of Adjustments. It sits on third Thursdays at City Hall and wants applications by the 25th of the month. Planning staff will book a time to talk through your request.

Yes, though you should disclose them. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, and a lender may insist on a fix first. Ask planning staff what the city's file shows for the address.

  • Camp Creek Marketplace has more than a million square feet of commercial and retail space.
  • Camp Creek Business Center and South Meadow Business Park supply nearby jobs.
  • Sumner Park holds a velodrome the city says is the only one in the state.
  • Annual downtown events include the Taste of East Point and a Fourth of July fireworks celebration.

Pick the lines that fit your street. A buyer from farther out will react to the airport and MARTA distances, while a buyer who wants a porch and a walk to dinner cares about the downtown blocks.

Who bills property tax on an East Point house

Two governments bill an East Point house separately: the City of East Point and Fulton County. The city's Finance Department collects city tax and runs city homestead exemptions. Valuations come from the Fulton County Board of Assessors, and the city council sets the city millage rate.

The city's tax year follows the calendar, statements are generally mailed in the fall, and the due date, 60 days after mailing, appears on each statement. The state also approved a one-time 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant that lowers assessed taxable value by up to $18,000 for homes with an approved homestead exemption. The credit posts to the city bill without a separate application, and it excludes rental, commercial and personal property.

Fulton County mailed its 2026 Notices of Assessment in June, and owners have 45 days from the notice to appeal the value. In October 2026 the county commissioners held the general fund rate at 8.87 mills, its fifth straight year without a change.

  • City bill, payment and city exemption: East Point Finance.
  • Value, exemption records and appeals: Fulton County assessors.
  • Dividing this year's taxes with the buyer: your closing attorney.

Short-term rental permits and a sale

Ask the Planning and Community Development Department whether a short-term rental permit carries over to a new owner before you promise a buyer anything. The city requires its permit before any listing appears on Airbnb or VRBO, and it renews each year.

The city treats a rental of 29 days or less as short term. It lists a $75 homestay license and a $150 whole-house lodging license, and it collects an 8 percent hotel/motel tax, with each month's tax due on the 20th of the next. Whole-house rentals are limited to a short list of zoning districts, including R1A, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-T and CR. East Point reported 65 permitted short-term rentals in 2025. Ordinance violations draw fines of $50 to $1,000 per offense, and every day a violation continues can count again.

If you operated a rental, gather your permit, your tax filings and any complaint history. Whoever buys will want proof that the address is in good standing.

Georgia transfer tax at closing

Georgia taxes the transfer itself, and the tax has to be paid before a deed can be recorded. The sales contract names who covers it.

State law puts the liability on the seller, and plenty of contracts hand it to the buyer. A declaration form, PT-61, goes in electronically at closing. Questions about exemptions go to the clerk of superior court for Fulton County.

Ask the closing attorney for an itemized seller statement ahead of time. It should list your mortgage payoff, the prorated city and county taxes, the transfer tax if it is yours, and any balances the city shows against the address.

When an investor offer makes sense

An investor offer helps most when delay is costing you. In East Point that usually means a house that sat vacant after an inheritance, a rental whose tenant stopped paying, a short-term rental you no longer want to operate, or a house needing repairs that a mortgage lender's appraiser would flag.

  • You want to name the closing day yourself.
  • The roof, plumbing or foundation needs work you will not finance.
  • You live out of state or are settling an estate from a distance.

Weigh any offer against what a repaired listing might net after commission and repair bills. Get the number in writing, see which closing costs fall on you, and treat the right to refuse as non-negotiable.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Georgia seller have to fix East Point house problems before a cash sale?

No repair is required for a cash buyer who agrees to take the house in its present state. A buyer who uses a mortgage may negotiate repairs after the inspection or appraisal.

Who is liable for the real estate transfer tax on an East Point sale?

The seller carries it by default under state law, yet contracts often assign it to the buyer. Payment comes before recording of the deed.

Where do I look up an East Point property tax account?

Use the Property Tax Search on the City of East Point site for the city bill and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner for the county bill. Assessment notices and exemption records are at fultonassessor.org.

Will the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant reduce tax on my rental house?

No. The grant is limited to homeowners with an approved 2026 homestead exemption. It posts as a credit on the city bill, and it does not apply to rental property.

Is it a problem to sell an East Point house while tenants live there?

It is common. With 43.6 percent of homes owner occupied, East Point has many rentals. Review the lease and deposit, and tell every prospective buyer that the unit is occupied.

Is a quick sale right for your Kennesaw house?

A quick sale fits Kennesaw owners who face repairs, an estate to settle or a payment problem, while a full listing suits those with time and a tidy house. The 2025 estimate for the city is 37,970 residents, against 33,036 counted in 2020. That growth keeps buyers active, though it also puts many listings near the university and along Cobb Parkway.

Speed matters most when a house needs work, sits empty or carries a loan you cannot keep paying. In those cases weigh the closing date and repair bill against the price. Write down the net under each route before choosing one.

Kennesaw sits in a county with its own tax office, so deeds and bills involve both Cobb County and the city.

Kennesaw homes and household numbers

Kennesaw covers about 9.5 square miles in northwest Cobb County. U.S. 41 and State Route 3 run through town as Cobb Parkway, and Interstate 75 clips the northeast corner with exits 269, 271 and 273. Downtown Atlanta is about 27 miles southeast. Houses a short drive from the I-75 exits are the easiest for a buyer to place on a map.

For 2020 to 2024 there are 13,554 households here, 64.6 percent of them owner occupied. Median home value is $335,400 and median gross rent is $1,845. Renting is an option if you inherit and prefer not to sell right away.

  • Median household income: $83,356 (in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 28.6 minutes

What drives buyer demand

Kennesaw State University is the biggest anchor, so ask a local agent how much nearby demand ties back to the campus. The Southern Museum of Civil War and Locomotive History downtown and the Kennesaw Mountain battlefield park, with about 18 miles of trails, draw visitors all year. The Big Shanty Festival each April brings crowds downtown.

Mentioning the trails and the downtown depot in a listing gives walkable-history buyers a reason to look.

Humid summers wear on roofs, gutters, crawl spaces and exterior paint, so a buyer's inspector will start with drainage, moisture and the age of the HVAC system. Selling as is, expect those items to set the price. Listing instead, a modest round of fixes to flashing, grading and mechanicals often costs less than the discount requested after inspection.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Kennesaw house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Who bills property tax and when it is due

Kennesaw owners get two tax bills. Cobb County collects for itself and the school district, and the city runs a separate city bill. The county values property at 40 percent of market value. City bills are mailed October 1 and carry a December 1 due date.

The city's tax covers the full year with no proration, so sharing the bill with a buyer is a contract term. Before signing, ask your closing attorney how each of the two bills will show on the settlement statement.

Kennesaw tax bills and who handles them
Bill or stepOfficeTiming or rule
County and school taxCobb Tax CommissionerBills go out in August with an October due date
City of Kennesaw taxCity Finance DepartmentMailed October 1, due December 1 each year
Value and appealsCobb Board of Tax Assessors45 days after the notice date
Senior city exemptionCity Finance DepartmentOwner 65 or older by January 1, apply by April 1

Unpaid Kennesaw city taxes

Interest begins the morning after the due date. The city then layers on a 5 percent penalty at 120 days and a further 5 percent every 120 days after that, stopping at 20 percent of principal. It also runs an annual tax sale on the first Tuesday in November at City Hall, starting at 9:00 AM, advertised in the Marietta Daily Journal four weeks beforehand.

Pay off any open city or county balance before you take an offer. Title work will find it, and the payoff would otherwise be taken from what you receive.

Selling a house that ran as an Airbnb

It can be sold, though the rental permission may stay behind. The city's short-term rental ordinance (Chapter 22, Article XIII) covers any dwelling let for fewer than 30 consecutive days and calls for both a city business license and a Short-Term Rental Certificate, which expires every December 31. The application fee is $250.

A house operating before January 1, 2025 could register as nonconforming, but that status ends automatically when ownership changes. A new owner who wants nightly guests must meet the current rules: the 8 percent hotel and motel excise tax, the two-property maximum and the 250-foot distance requirement that nonconforming rentals skip. Explain this to buyers early. The Business License Office is at 3080 Moon Station Road.

Permits and records

Open permits cause the most trouble, so ask the city's building and inspections staff whether any permit on the house was left unclosed. Unfinished work from a past owner can stall a buyer with a loan even when a cash buyer would take it as is. Cobb County Fire covers the city, while Kennesaw keeps its own police department and 9-1-1 center at City Hall.

  • Collect permit records and receipts for roof, HVAC and electrical jobs.
  • Confirm no city or county tax balance is outstanding.
  • For a former rental, ask the Business License Office which registrations are still active.

Georgia's transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. It is paid before the deed is recorded.

Steps for a quick Kennesaw sale

Whichever buyer you choose, the order of work is similar. First, collect the deed, any estate papers and your loan payoff figure. Second, check the city and county tax balances, because two bills means two places a balance can hide. Third, ask the city about open permits and, for a former rental, about the business license and certificate. Fourth, get written offers and compare the net under each one.

A cash buyer can often close faster because there is no lender to satisfy. A listed sale can bring a higher price, but it adds showings, an inspection and a loan approval. If you have a deadline, such as a foreclosure notice or an estate date, tell every buyer up front so they can say honestly whether they can meet it.

Keep copies of every offer, and do not sign anything until you have read the closing costs and the date the buyer must close by.

Frequently asked questions

How soon could a cash sale close in Kennesaw?

Timing rests on the title search and the buyer, but a cash deal skips underwriting and the lender's appraisal, usually the slowest steps. Leave room for title work and for the transfer tax filing with the Clerk of Superior Court.

Do Cobb and Kennesaw send separate tax bills?

Yes. Cobb bills county and school taxes, and the city mails its own bill October 1 with a December 1 due date. Because the city does not prorate, the split with a buyer is set in your contract.

Is it worth appealing a Cobb assessment before a sale?

Only if the value looks high and the window is open. Owners get 45 days from the date printed on the Notice of Assessment.

Will my homestead exemption follow the house to a buyer?

No. The exemption depends on you owning and living in the home on January 1. Kennesaw also offers its own city exemption for owners 65 and older, applied for by April 1.

Can I sell a Kennesaw house that needs a new roof?

Yes, as is. Expect the offer to reflect the repair cost, and keep permit records on hand so the buyer's inspection and title review go smoothly.

Your selling options in Tucker

Tucker owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a direct offer from a buyer who purchases houses in their current condition. The city sits inside DeKalb County, so assessment, tax billing and deed recording for any sale run through county offices.

  • An agent listing reaches the most buyers, though showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval stretch the calendar.
  • A sale by owner keeps price and terms in your hands, along with the contract and disclosure work.
  • A direct buyer skips financing contingencies and repair requests, and the offer usually lands below a fully renovated listing price.

Whichever way you go, collect the deed, your mortgage payoff figure, any open permit paperwork and HOA covenants before the first conversation. Most of the delay in a Georgia sale comes from documents that could have been prepared in advance.

Is your address in the city?

Tucker has widened its borders since 2016, which is unusual for a metro Atlanta city. Land area grew from 11.98 square miles in 2010 to 20.20 square miles in 2020. Homeowners along Livsey Drive petitioned to join in September 2016, and the Wanda Woods and Westwood subdivisions followed on January 1, 2017. Briarcliff Village Shopping Center was annexed in 2018, and a year later much of the neighboring Northlake Mall came in too.

A petition needs property touching the current boundary, and the mayor and council must approve it by majority vote. For a seller, the practical point is that your street may sit just across a line. Ask City Hall, or check the city map, to confirm whether the house is in the city or in unincorporated DeKalb County, because that decides which permit desk and code officers you deal with.

Tucker housing numbers

Owners live in 63.0 percent of Tucker's homes. Unless a label gives a date, each figure below is a 2020 to 2024 estimate.

Schools buyers ask about

Tucker's cluster schools belong to the DeKalb County School District. Five neighborhood elementary schools feed Tucker Middle School, and Tucker Middle feeds Tucker High School, which has won state football and basketball championships. The district has been running a student assignment project, so zones may shift. Check the assigned schools for your exact address with the district office before you put anything about schools in writing.

  • Look up the attendance zone for your address on the district site.
  • Name the cluster in your listing or your pitch to a buyer, once the district has confirmed it.
  • Keep a copy of the zone confirmation in your sale file.

Permits, code rules and business licenses

Unpermitted work, code violations and covenant restrictions cause most hiccups. Tucker's Building and Permitting Division reviews plans, issues permits and conducts inspections, and permits can be submitted electronically.

The city lists water heater replacement, water or sewer line replacement, electrical service upgrades, panel changes and air conditioner change outs as work that needs a permit. Paint, minor non-structural repairs such as glass panes and door hardware, and detached non-habitable structures under 200 square feet do not. Subdivision covenants may still apply, so ask your homeowners association first.

Code Enforcement aims for voluntary compliance. Typical examples are an inoperable vehicle parked on private property and outdoor storage, both of which can be fixed in a weekend before a buyer walks through.

If you run a business from the house, the city requires an occupational tax certificate for every for-profit business, home-based ones included. Renewals fall due January 1 and turn delinquent after April 15. The licensing line at City Hall is (678) 597-9040.

How to appeal your DeKalb valuation

DeKalb sets a value as of January 1 each year and taxes 40 percent of fair market value. Once the notice goes out, you have 45 days to appeal.

The county's property search tool displays current and past values, lets you download notices, and accepts an online appeal using the access code from your notice. A mailed appeal goes to the Property Appraisal Department, 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, and should include the parcel number, your reason, your evidence and which appeal route you choose.

  • Board of Equalization: free, heard by a three-member panel of property owners.
  • Hearing Officer: for properties over $500,000 that are not homesteaded, with no filing fee.
  • Non-binding arbitration: needs a certified appraisal you pay for, plus a $217 filing fee.

The appeal matters to a seller while you still hold title, because the buyer inherits the final value. Bills themselves come from the DeKalb Tax Commissioner's Office.

Closing, transfer tax and land use

Georgia will not let a deed be recorded until its transfer tax is paid, and the Department of Revenue page prints the rate. The seller owes it by default, and the contract may move it to the buyer. The declaration is Form PT-61, filed online through the clerks' cooperative authority, whose support lines are (800) 304-5174 and (404) 327-9760. For exemption questions, the state sends you to the county clerk.

Land use questions have their own channel. Tucker has a Planning Commission, a Zoning Board of Appeals and a Construction Board of Appeals, plus a land use petition directory for rezoning and variance requests. Ask Planning and Zoning at (678) 597-9040 before promising a buyer that a lot can be split or a use changed.

In a cash sale there is no lender appraisal or loan underwriting to wait on, so the closing steps are the title search, the payoff, the PT-61 and the recording. Have the deed and payoff figure on hand so the title company can start the search the day you accept.

Frequently asked questions

Is it possible to sell a Tucker house that needs work?

Yes. Sell it as is, hand it to an investor, or fix only the items that would block a buyer's loan. Open permits and unpermitted work are the problems most likely to surface, so check them with the city's Building and Permitting Division first.

Does replacing a water heater in Tucker need a permit?

Yes. The city names water heater replacement among its mechanical, electrical and plumbing permit examples. Have the contractor pull the permit so the inspection record is ready when a buyer asks.

Who owes the Georgia transfer tax in a Tucker sale?

State law makes the seller liable, though sales contracts often assign it to the buyer. Read that clause before signing, since the amount is set by the price and is due before the deed is recorded.

How much time does a DeKalb owner get to contest a value?

Forty-five days, counted from the date printed on the notice. File through the county property search with the notice's access code, or mail a written appeal to the Property Appraisal Department in Decatur.

Are all Tucker-area addresses inside the city?

No. The city has annexed neighborhoods and commercial areas since 2016, and nearby addresses may still be in unincorporated DeKalb County. City Hall or the city map will tell you which side of the line your house is on.

Sale routes for a Hinesville house

Hinesville owners choose between a broker listing, a sale they run themselves and an investor's cash bid, and a move set by military orders often settles the choice. As the seat of Liberty County, the city sends deed, tax and assessment questions to county offices.

Pull together the deed, your latest Liberty County tax bill, the payoff figure and any orders or lease dates that fix your timeline. With those in hand, a buyer or attorney can quote real numbers fast.

Hinesville housing figures

How Fort Stewart shapes the market

Hinesville is about forty miles southwest of Savannah, next to Fort Stewart, and has been the Liberty County seat since 1837. The post began in 1940 as a training site named Camp Stewart and was designated a fort in 1956. The city has grown from about 4,000 residents in the 1970s to 34,891 in the 2020 count, and its fortunes track the post.

That link shows up in everyday utilities. The wastewater treatment plant on Fort Stewart opened in 1984 and serves both the installation and city customers. A Utility Clearinghouse office opened on post in the 1990s to make opening and closing utility accounts easier during PCS and TCS moves. A buyer relocating from the post will care about that, so mention it.

Liberty County assessments and homestead filings

The Liberty County Board of Assessors values each property and mails an Annual Notice of Assessment, mostly in May. The notice is not a bill. An appeal must come within 45 days of the notice date, and a high tax amount alone is not grounds.

  • Homestead filing: January 1 to April 1.
  • Real property return: January 1 to April 1.
  • Assessment notices go out: May of each year.
  • Time to appeal: 45 days after the notice.
  • Personal property returns mailed: December 22 yearly.

The homestead cutoff is firm. Completed applications must be postmarked or received by 5 PM on April 1 to count for that tax year, and the forms come from the Georgia Department of Revenue. The owner must hold title to land and house and live there. After a purchase, a homestead filing, a return, an appeal or a permit, an appraiser may inspect the property, and appraisal staff are allowed to walk the outside of a property under Georgia Code 48-5-264.1.

Which offices touch a Hinesville sale?

The Liberty County Tax Commissioner bills real estate tax, the Clerk of Courts holds deeds, and the City of Hinesville runs inspections, code enforcement and business licenses. Each answers a different question.

Have your closing attorney show how this year's Liberty County tax is divided with the buyer. Georgia's transfer tax, owed before recording, is a separate line to check in the contract.

What to bring to the office

A few documents save repeat trips. For the tax commissioner, bring your parcel number or bill number and photo identification. For the assessors, bring the Annual Notice of Assessment if you plan to appeal or to ask about a homestead filing. For Inspections, bring the address and any permit paperwork from past work on the house.

If you are selling for cash, the buyer's title company will pull most of these records itself, but having your own copies lets you spot a problem first. A balance you did not know about is far easier to settle before a contract than after.

When orders keep you away, a trusted person with the right authority paperwork can handle these visits for you. Ask your closing attorney what that paperwork should say.

Planning a sale when you have orders

Orders turn a sale into a deadline job. Count back from your report date and decide early whether a listing can close before you go.

  • Set a latest acceptable closing date in writing before you list.

Forty-five days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, which is mailed mostly in May. The appeal addresses value, since a high tax amount alone is not grounds.

Yes. Call the Hinesville Inspections Department to learn whether any permit or code note is open on the address, and clear it up before a buyer's inspector finds it.

A Utility Clearinghouse opened on Fort Stewart in the 1990s to ease opening and closing accounts for PCS and TCS moves. Call the city to confirm how it works today.

State law makes the seller liable, though many contracts assign it to the buyer. Payment comes before the deed is recorded.

How does Henry County property tax work for a Stockbridge seller?

The Henry County tax commissioner sends each bill to the January 1 owner, with payment due by November 16. Late balances accrue interest and penalties under a schedule printed in the county's FAQ, and a mailed payment needs a USPS postmark.

A sale that closes mid-year needs one extra step. Under Georgia Code 48-3-3, a lien lands on the January 1 owner unless the county receives a settlement statement showing where the taxes were paid within 90 days after the due date. Henry County wants page one of that statement and the property address, sent to its property tax email.

Fees can surprise a seller. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation charges ride on the same bill, and a county water charge pays for pipes and storage even if a house has a well. The departments named on the bill answer questions about each fee.

Homestead and appeal deadlines

Homestead applications in Henry County are due April 1 and can be made online or at either tax office, one on Burke Street in Stockbridge and the main office on Henry Parkway in McDonough. Owners who have fallen behind face tax sales that the county runs on the first Tuesday of each month, starting at 10:00 AM at the McDonough office on Henry Parkway.

Before a Stockbridge deed is recorded, the state's transfer tax has to be paid. The seller bears it unless the contract names the buyer, and the Department of Revenue lists the current rate on its transfer tax page. An online PT-61 form reports the sale.

The firm that closes your sale normally files the form, retires the mortgage and records the deed. Request a written payoff and a draft settlement statement several days early, and compare its tax line with the Henry County bill. Mortgage payoff figures change by the day, so ask the servicer for a good-through date and confirm the number again just before you sign. If the house is held by more than one owner, each one signs, and each needs time to review the statement. Ask the closing office to send the statement to everyone at the same time.

Do these in order and a cash sale or a listing both move faster, since most delays come from a missing payoff, an unpaid bill or an unrecorded paper. A tidy file also helps you judge offers fairly, because you will know what you owe before a buyer asks.

Is Stockbridge in Henry County?

Yes. The Henry County Tax Commissioner bills property tax for Stockbridge parcels and keeps an office on Burke Street, and Henry County Schools operate the public schools.

When are Henry County property taxes due?

November 16 is the due date, and the bill goes to whoever held the property on January 1. Interest and penalties start after that date, as the county's FAQ explains.

What happens to the tax bill if I sell my Stockbridge house mid-year?

The bill still goes to the January 1 owner. If the county has not received a settlement statement showing where the taxes were paid within 90 days after the due date, it files a lien against that owner.

Do I need to pay a transfer tax to sell in Stockbridge?

Yes, unless an exemption applies. The state collects it before the deed is recorded, and the seller owes it unless the contract says otherwise. The Department of Revenue's transfer tax page states the rate.

Can I sell a house in Stockbridge that needs repairs?

Yes. Plenty of buyers take houses as they are and reduce the price by the repair bill. Weigh two or more offers against what fixing the house yourself would cost.

Forty-five days from the date on the notice of change, in writing, to the Board of Tax Assessors. The appeal can rest on taxability, value or uniformity, and it cannot be a complaint about the amount of tax.

You need clear authority before any buyer can close, and the estate representative has to sign. Ask the closing attorney what documents the title company will require, then set the closing date.

Dalton is the Whitfield County seat, in the Blue Ridge foothills beside Interstate 75. Locals call it the Carpet Capital of the World. When mills downsized, Dalton lost 4,600 jobs from June 2011 to June 2012, and a Qcells solar panel factory opened in 2019, with an expansion completed on October 18, 2023.

I-75 runs a short way west, U.S. 41 and U.S. 76 bypass the center, and State Route 52 crosses downtown. The city has an estimated 35,322 residents for July 2025 on 21.14 square miles of land, and more than 20 parks and playgrounds. Rocky Face Ridge and Haig Mill Lake Park offer trails nearby.

Dalton's Code Enforcement unit applies the International Property Maintenance Code to dangerous or dilapidated buildings, overgrown or littered lots, inoperable vehicles, trash, illegal dumping and disrepair. Residents report violations through SeeClickFix, or by email to code@daltonga.gov or by phone at 706-529-8769.

The city asks for a building permit before any construction, repair, move, removal or demolition of a structure, with a separate permit for each electrical, plumbing and mechanical job. Nothing begins until the permit is issued.

The seller is liable under the state's rules, though the contract can pass the cost along. Recording follows payment.

Typically yes for structural work and for electrical, plumbing or mechanical jobs, each with its own permit, issued before work starts.

The city's code enforcement staff, who coordinate with public works, police, fire and building inspectors. Write to code@daltonga.gov with questions.

Buyers who commute care about access, and LaGrange has it: Interstates 85 and 185, U.S. 27 and 29, and Georgia 219 and 109 all pass through. An EF2 tornado hit the southern half of LaGrange on January 12, 2023. If your house was in or near that path, buyers will likely ask about roof work, fallen trees and any claims filed afterward.

  • Request a claims history from your insurer if a buyer asks for it.

Documented repairs cost far less in negotiation than unexplained patches. Buyers paying cash still want to see receipts.

When Troup County tax bills come due

The county's Tax Commissioner sets November 15 as the yearly deadline, with penalties and interest after that. Value is fixed as of January 1 at 40 percent of what the property is worth, and the tax equals that assessed value times a millage rate set by the school board, the county and any other taxing body.

Troup's Board of Assessors is appointed by the county commissioners but runs on its own. To learn whether a city levy applies to your parcel, call the Tax Commissioner at 706-883-1620.

File an appeal against the Annual Assessment Notice inside a 45-day window that runs from the notice date. The right is lost afterward. The appeal goes either to a hearing before the Board of Equalization, whose members are chosen by the grand jury and who charge nothing, or to arbitration, where each side pays its own arbitrator and half the cost of a third.

Appeal only if the value looks well above what similar houses bring. The assessment does not set your sale price, but a lower one trims the tax a buyer will carry.

Code rules and permits in the city

The city follows the state's mandatory minimum codes, and effective January 1, 2026 these include the 2024 International Residential Code and Building Code with Georgia amendments. Ask Community Development about any job started under an earlier code year.

Code enforcement sits within the LaGrange police department, and officers deal with overgrown grass and weeds, litter, abandoned or inoperable vehicles, nuisances and sewage problems. The goal is voluntary compliance, so on a vacant or inherited house keep the grass cut and the exterior clear. Find out about any open notice before you sign.

Deed transfer tax

Georgia charges $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 of the price, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. The contract can shift the payment to the buyer, and recording waits until it is paid.

Begin with the paperwork: the deed, your payoff figure, and the latest Troup County tax notice. Call the Tax Commissioner at 706-883-1620 to confirm the balance and whether a city levy applies. Then collect offers. A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal and often closes on a date you choose, while a listing may bring a higher price after repairs and showings. Compare the net from each, and schedule a final reading and transfer for your city utility accounts.

It can, once the tenant situation is clear. Landlords often prefer a quick cash closing on a rental needing work, and with most local homes renter occupied, investors are active. Get lease terms in writing first.

November 15 each year. Penalties and interest begin after that date, and the Tax Commissioner's office answers questions at 706-883-1620.

How much time do I get to contest a Troup assessment?

Forty-five days from the date shown on the Annual Assessment Notice. After that, the right to appeal that year's value is gone.

When is the Troup homestead filing period?

January 1 through April 1. Skipping it waives the exemption for that year, and the house must be your residence and owned by you on January 1.

Do I need to close my LaGrange utility accounts when selling?

Yes, arrange it with the city. LaGrange itself supplies electricity, gas, water, sewer and refuse service, so schedule a final reading and move the accounts to the new owner.

It is 3.26 mills, or $3.26 for each $1,000 of assessed value. That covers the city levy only, not county or school taxes.

April 1. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and an approved exemption stays in place without yearly reapplication.

Usually, with the balance taken from proceeds at closing. Georgia law allows a FiFa lien on unpaid tax, so settle it before accepting an offer.

How can a Pooler owner sell quickly?

A direct cash sale moves fastest. A full-price listing that waits on a financed buyer moves slowest, with a private sale somewhere between. Pooler owners usually weigh the condition of the house, their own deadline and how much money they would put into prep.

Location helps here. Pooler calls itself the commercial center of west Chatham County, at the crossing of Interstates 95 and 16, about ten miles west of Savannah and within two miles of Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport. Pooler grew from 19,140 residents in 2010 to 25,711 at the 2020 count, and the mid-2025 estimate is 32,744. Much of that growth is recent, so many houses are newer than those in nearby older towns. The city's 2016 to 2040 Comprehensive Plan, adopted October 18, 2021, shows how Pooler is thinking about land and water. It lists strategies such as evaluating a two-foot freeboard for flood protection in development, an updated stormwater ordinance covering floodway impacts, an impaired waters ordinance, a sea level rise checklist for development projects, and a historic preservation ordinance. How do Chatham County assessments and exemptions work?

To qualify for homestead, you must own the home and treat it as your permanent residence on January 1. Rentals are excluded, and an immediate family group can exempt just one house. The owner files in person unless someone holds a power of attorney, and staff ask to see a Georgia driver's license or ID card and vehicle registrations.

No deed gets recorded until the state transfer tax is paid. The statewide clerks' cooperative treats that tax as an excise on the sale and hosts the PT-61 form online.

A Pooler deed is recorded in Chatham County by the settlement office you hire. Ask who pays the tax under your contract. Ask for the closing statement a day or two early so you can check the mortgage payoff, any tax owed and any association dues.

If the house sits in a subdivision, also ask the association for a statement of dues, since unpaid dues can hold up the sale. A cash sale usually closes through the same kind of settlement office, so these same checks apply whichever route you pick.

When is a cash offer the better fit in Pooler?

Cash works best when a conventional sale would stall. Pooler owners often reach for it in these cases:

  • A rental house whose tenants left it worn out, or whose lease limits showings.
  • A relocation with a start date at a new job that will not wait for a lender's approval.
  • A house with water damage, an older roof or a failed inspection that scared off a financed buyer.
  • An estate sale where several heirs want the money without managing repairs.

  5. Request the closing statement early and check the payoff, taxes and association dues.

A cash buyer will still want most of these papers. Having them ready shortens the time between an offer and a closing, and it lets you compare offers on the same footing instead of guessing at what each one leaves out.

Is Pooler a good market for a quick sale?

It can be. The city sits at the junction of two interstates ten miles from Savannah, and the population has grown steadily since 2010. Condition and price still decide how fast a particular house sells.

Where does a Pooler homeowner apply for homestead?

File with the Chatham County Board of Assessors at 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue, Suite 113, in Savannah. Bring a Georgia driver's license or identification card and vehicle registrations, and apply in person unless you have given someone a power of attorney.

Does the buyer keep my exemption after the sale?

No. Automatic renewal applies only to the home and owner originally exempted, so the next owner applies on their own. If they file by the appeal due date on the notice, it counts for that tax year.

The Planning and Zoning Commission only advises, and its recommendations do not bind City Council. It meets monthly at City Hall, so ask the planning department how your lot is zoned before you sell.

What must be filed for a deed to be recorded?

The PT-61 has to be filed and the tax paid before recording. The form is filled out online and printed, and whoever runs your closing normally submits it with the deed.

Chamblee sits in northern DeKalb County, northeast of Atlanta, with Dunwoody to the north, Doraville to the northeast and Brookhaven to the southwest. It was incorporated in 1907. Annexations in 2010 and 2013 pulled in areas such as Huntley Hills and Beverly Hills and widened the city sharply.

After the war, the General Motors plant in neighboring Doraville and factories along Peachtree Industrial Boulevard brought workers, and the Buford Highway corridor, sometimes called the International Corridor, filled with shops. Several Chamblee neighborhoods have an identifiable housing type, and a buyer or investor will ask which one yours belongs to.

  • Sexton Woods and Keswick Village: 1950s ranch homes mixed with newer craftsman infill, next to Keswick Park.
  • Huntley Hills: a neighborhood started in the early 1960s, annexed in 2010, built around Huntley Hills Elementary.
  • Beverly Hills and Beverly Woods: mid-century ranch and split-level houses first built for General Motors workers, annexed in 2013.
  • Clairmont Park: residential streets along Clairmont Road near the airport.

A cash buyer pays without a mortgage, so the sale skips the appraisal, the lender's underwriting and the repair negotiation that usually follows an inspection. Chamblee's planning staff issue building, land disturbance and plat permits and also handle code compliance and the Design Review Board. Filing is online, and City Hall's ground floor has a desk for those who need help.

A first residential plan review takes roughly five business days. Fences and decks always require permits, and a shed bigger than 200 square feet needs an accessory structure permit. Skipping a permit can lead to a violation notice, a stop-work order and added fees.

Fifteen zoning districts apply across the city, each with its own permitted uses, and the interactive zoning map shows yours. A zoning verification letter lists a parcel's zoning description and past cases. The department's number is (770) 986-5010.

Location and market context

Union City is a small community in the southern part of Fulton County, roughly fifteen minutes from Atlanta and ten miles from Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport. Buyers who commute or fly often value that airport distance. Atlanta Metro Studios, one of the region's large production facilities, is also in the city.

Population has climbed from 19,456 in 2010 to 26,830 in 2020, with an estimate of 29,910 for July 1, 2025. Land area barely changed, 19.11 square miles in 2010 and 19.67 in 2020, so the new households arrived inside a nearly fixed footprint. Demand for housing here is real.

Property tax billing

Fulton splits the work in two. The Board of Assessors keeps ownership and mailing records, sets values and takes homestead applications and appeals. The Tax Commissioner builds the bill and collects payment.

How to appeal your Fulton assessment

Owners get 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment. Notices are posted online in June, and the notice itself shows your exact deadline, so read it the day it arrives.

Only the assessed value can be appealed, and the estimated tax cannot. File online at the county assessor site, in person or by mail, then pick a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on value, or a Hearing Officer, where fees may apply for the last two. Appeals can take months, and a temporary tax bill may arrive during the wait. Pay it, or penalties follow.

The South Fulton Service Center of the Board of Assessors sits at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224, and the phone is 404-612-6440. The standard homestead deadline is April 1, with a second window during the appeal period for owners who qualified as of January 1.

Permits and code enforcement

Most construction needs a building permit from the city, and work starts only once it is issued. A permit lapses when construction fails to begin within 180 days or stops for 180 consecutive days.

Permit applications, plan submittals, invoice payment and inspection scheduling run through the city's IWORQ online portal. Code Enforcement accepts violations by phone, fax, email or area survey, and an officer investigates within 24 hours of a report. Its phone line is (770) 515-7890, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Officers inspecting one property may also survey adjacent properties, so a neighbor's complaint can lead to a look at your yard.

The Planning Division posts the current zoning ordinance, development regulations and subdivision regulations, along with the Comprehensive Plan and Future Land Use Map. Look up the zoning on your parcel if a buyer plans a particular use.

The deed goes to the Fulton County Clerk of Superior Court once Georgia's transfer tax is paid. The seller is liable unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The state's printed rate sits on its Department of Revenue page.

Fulton County Schools serves Union City. Its South Learning Center is at 4025 Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district publishes an address lookup showing the elementary, middle and high school zones for any home. Share that result when a buyer asks.

If taxes or a code citation turn up during the title search, they get paid or cleared from your proceeds at closing. Raising them yourself before you list avoids a surprise at the table.

A rough order of events for a quick sale: collect your documents, confirm the tax and permit status with the offices above, accept an offer, open title, pay off the lender and any city balance, then sign and record the deed. A cash buyer shortens the middle of that list because there is no loan approval to wait for.

Tenants change the picture. If someone is renting the house, tell every bidder up front, hand over the lease, and agree on whether it will be sold occupied or delivered empty.

No sale inspection is part of the permit process. The city does require permits for most construction and runs inspections through the online portal, so confirm that past work was permitted and signed off.

What if I miss the Fulton assessment appeal deadline?

You lose the right to appeal that year's value once the printed date passes. Watch the date on each year's notice, which gives 45 days, and file early online or at a Board of Assessors office.

Can I report a code problem next door before I list?

Yes. Reports go in by phone at (770) 515-7890, fax, email or through an area survey during an inspection, and an officer looks into it within 24 hours. Clearing an eyesore early helps showings.

Fulton County Schools. Its South Learning Center is on Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district's address lookup shows the elementary, middle and high school zones for your house.

Property tax when you sell mid-year

The year's tax is tied to the owner of record on January 1, but after a later sale the county sends a bill to both buyer and seller. The earlier owner stays liable unless paperwork proving a transfer of liability reaches the commissioner within 90 days after the due date. Late payment adds penalties and interest. If the closing falls near the due date, ask the closing attorney to say in writing who is paying the bill.

The same January 1 test applies to homestead: the home must be both owned and lived in on that date. Applications are accepted year-round, but one that misses the deadline printed on the assessment notice waits for the next year. Owners 65 or older, or 100 percent disabled, may also claim a senior school exemption if income stays under a limit. Gwinnett appears on the state's list of valuation-freeze counties. Within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The county mails notices in May or June and prints your deadline on the notice.

The January 1 owner stays liable unless proof of a liability transfer reaches the tax commissioner within 90 days of the due date. After a later sale, both parties receive a bill.

The seller owes it by default, and the contract can shift it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue's transfer tax page gives the rate.

The Board of Regents picked the Carrollton campus on April 15, 1933, and it became West Georgia College, then the State University of West Georgia in 1996 and the University of West Georgia on January 12, 2005.

Rates come from several bodies: commissioners for county operations, the school board for schools, and the state, capped at a quarter mill.

An appeal begins at the county assessors' board and may continue to the Board of Equalization, a panel the grand jury appoints. You can choose arbitration instead. Carroll County. Its assessors set the values, and the county tax commissioner prepares bills, collects payment and answers questions at 770-830-5843.

  • A mortgage in arrears with a lender deadline approaching.
  • A rental with turnover or tenant trouble the owner no longer wants to manage.
  • A code complaint or lapsed permit likely to slow a financed buyer's inspection.

Forty-five days after you receive the notice of change. Send a written appeal to the assessors. If they hold the value, the file moves to the Board of Equalization, or you can choose arbitration instead.

No. Houston County renews an exemption automatically only for the same owner, so a change of ownership ends it. The new owner applies by April 1 of the first year they want the exemption.

The boundary also changes senior tax breaks. Bartow's assessors list $60,000 off school taxes at 65 for the city system, while the county system gets $60,000 at 65, $80,000 at 75 and $200,000 at 80, each judged on January 1. Ask the assessors which system covers your parcel.

Due dates and penalties

Bartow taxes a home on 40 percent of the value its assessors choose, and its Tax Commissioner bills for the county, the schools and the cities inside the county. Real estate bills are due November 15, gain 1 percent monthly interest after that, and take a 10 percent penalty past 90 days.

Left unpaid for over 30 days, a bill can become a fifa recorded at the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus can read it. Call the Tax Commissioner at (770) 387-5111 for a payoff figure before closing so a lien does not stall the deal.

Homestead credit and ownership date

  • Homestead credit: an occupant on January 1 may deduct $15,000 of assessed value for county and county school taxes.
  • Filing time: by April 1, or within the 45 days after notices are mailed.
  • Online ownership: a January 1 snapshot, so a spring purchase appears under the buyer's name when the digest posts in September.

Anything filed later counts for the following year, and the house must have been your home on January 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cartersville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

To challenge a value, complete form PT-311A within 45 days of the notice. Email it to assessors@bartowcountyga.gov, fax it, mail it to 135 W. Cherokee Ave Ste 126 or drop it at the courthouse office. Give your opinion of value, add comparable sales and pick a route, usually the Board of Equalization. A high bill alone is not a ground.

After the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator rules, a further step to Superior Court needs filing within 30 days, plus a $25 clerk fee.

From offer to closing

The sequence is short. Settle on a price or accept an offer, choose a closing attorney, and request a payoff figure from the Tax Commissioner so no lien surprises anyone. The attorney runs the title work, files the PT-61, pays the transfer tax and records the deed with the Bartow clerk. With a cash buyer there is no lender review, so you and the buyer pick the date. With a financed buyer, expect an appraisal, an inspection and possibly a repair request before the date firms up.

Bring to the attorney's office your photo ID, the latest assessment notice, any lease, and permits for work done on the house. If you own the property with someone else or inherited it, mention that at the start so the paperwork matches who is on title.

Deed costs and recording

The transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 of price, plus 10 cents for each further $100, with fractions rounded up. The seller is liable, and contracts commonly pass the cost to the buyer.

Recording at the Bartow clerk's office waits for the tax, and the clerk then stamps proof on the deed. The PT-61 form is filed electronically, and the courthouse deed room can give you a copy of your own purchase deed.

City permits before you sell

Structural, electrical, plumbing or mechanical work inside the city goes through Planning and Development, the office that also covers zoning, code enforcement and business licenses.

The city's residential inspection list names the temporary power pole, footing, rough work, duplex and townhome fire walls, sprinkler checks by the fire marshal, insulation, temporary power and a final that spans all four trades, landscaping and required appliances. A certificate of occupancy also needs the Georgia Energy Code form, and engineer letters where foundation or compaction work called for them. Email inspections@cityofcartersville.org with the permit number, address, type and date, and expect a visit the next business day.

If a deck or basement finish went in without paperwork, ask the department how to correct it before a buyer's inspector notices. A cash buyer may accept that risk for a lower price.

Frequently asked questions

How quickly does a cash sale close in Cartersville?

On whatever date you and the buyer agree, because no lender has to approve the loan. The Bartow clerk records the deed after the transfer tax is paid, so leave time for title work.

Does the buyer or seller owe the transfer tax in Cartersville?

The seller, unless the contract moves the cost to the buyer.

What day is Bartow County's real estate tax due?

The bill is due November 15. Interest accrues monthly after that, and a penalty follows once 90 days pass.

Can I file for homestead after the April 1 date?

Yes, if you apply in the 45 days after assessment notices go out. Anything later counts for the following year, and the house must have been your home on January 1.

How do I challenge my Cartersville assessment?

Send form PT-311A inside the 45 days that follow the notice. Give your opinion of value, add comparable sales and pick a route, usually the Board of Equalization.
